postings.conferenceText: Sobre a CIETIA’27A CIETIA’27 – 1.ª Conferência Internacional sobre Educação, Tecnologias e Inteligência Artificial é um evento científico internacional promovido pela ALICE – Aliança Lusófona para a Investigação, Cooperação e Educação Digital, em coorganização com a Universidade Politécnica de Moçambique.Subordinada ao tema “Inteligência Artificial na Educação: Inovação, Desafios e Transformação Digital”, a conferência pretende reunir investigadores, docentes, estudantes, profissionais, decisores políticos e representantes de instituições de ensino, investigação, organizações e empresas, promovendo a divulgação científica, a partilha de conhecimento, a cooperação internacional e a inovação no domínio da educação digital.A CIETIA’27 constitui um espaço privilegiado para a apresentação e discussão de investigações científicas que contribuam para o avanço do conhecimento nas áreas da educação, das tecnologias digitais e da inteligência artificial, incentivando a criação de redes internacionais de investigação e o desenvolvimento de projetos colaborativos.A conferência decorrerá em formato híbrido (presencial e online), nos dias 14, 15 e 16 de abril de 2027, em Maputo, Moçambique.Orientações para SubmissãoTodos os trabalhos submetidos à CIETIA’27 deverão ser originais, inéditos e não poderão encontrar-se simultaneamente em processo de avaliação ou publicados noutra conferência, revista científica, livro ou qualquer outra publicação científica.São aceites submissões em português e inglês.A conferência aceita exclusivamente artigos completos, os quais deverão apresentar investigações concluídas ou em fase avançada de desenvolvimento, incluindo enquadramento teórico, revisão da literatura, metodologia, resultados, discussão, conclusões e referências bibliográficas.Os artigos deverão ser preparados de acordo com o modelo oficial da conferência e respeitar integralmente as normas de formatação disponibilizadas pela organização.Todos os trabalhos serão submetidos a um processo de avaliação científica por pares, em regime de dupla revisão cega (Double-Blind Peer Review).Os artigos serão avaliados de acordo com os seguintes critérios:Originalidade e relevância científica;Qualidade do enquadramento teórico e da revisão da literatura;Adequação e rigor metodológico;Qualidade da análise e discussão dos resultados;Clareza da redação e organização do artigo;Contributo científico para as áreas temáticas da conferência.Os artigos aceites serão apresentados durante a conferência e publicados nas respetivas Atas da CIETIA’27, mediante o cumprimento das normas editoriais e da inscrição de, pelo menos, um dos autores.Eixos Temáticos1. Inteligência Artificial e Tecnologias Emergentes na EducaçãoInteligência artificial generativa na educação;Learning analytics;Realidade virtual, aumentada e mista;Sistemas inteligentes de aprendizagem;Aplicações educativas.2. Educação Digital e Ambientes Virtuais de Aprendizageme-learning, b-learning, m-learning e MOOCs;Learning Management Systems (LMS);Ambientes virtuais de aprendizagem;Educação para a sustentabilidade;Tecnologias para a aprendizagem online.3. Inovação Pedagógica e Formação de ProfessoresMetodologias ativas de aprendizagem;Sistemas alternativos e aumentativos de comunicação;Competências digitais docentes;Formação inicial e contínua de docentes;Práticas educativas inovadoras e políticas curriculares;Estratégias de avaliação da aprendizagem.4. Ética, Qualidade e Investigação na Educação DigitalÉtica no uso das tecnologias digitais;Privacidade e proteção de dados;Acreditação e qualidade da educação;Cidadania digital e geopolítica das línguas;Investigação em tecnologias educativas.5. Transformação Digital, Governança e SociedadeInovação, transformação digital e social na educação;Políticas públicas e educativas;Novos desafios para o mercado do trabalho;Direitos humanos, inclusão, acessibilidade e diversidade;Cooperação e mobilidade académica.Comissão CientíficaA Comissão Científica da CIETIA’27 será constituída por investigadores e especialistas nacionais e internacionais de reconhecido mérito científico nas áreas da educação, das tecnologias digitais, da inteligência artificial, da inovação pedagógica e da transformação digital.A composição integral da Comissão Científica será divulgada oportunamente na página oficial da conferência.Comissão OrganizadoraA Comissão Organizadora da CIETIA’27 é constituída pelos seguintes membros:Amália Cutane Comiche, Instituto Superior de Ciências e Tecnologia de Moçambique;Ana Maria Pinho Guina, Universidade Politécnica – Campus de Nampula;Bruno Miguel Ferreira Gonçalves, Universidade Politécnica de Bragança;Celestino Lopes de Barros, Universidade de Cabo Verde;Clarisse Céu Pais, Universidade Politécnica de Bragança;Edson Filomeno Joaquim Rufai, Instituto Superior de Ciências e Tecnologia de Moçambique;Eurídice Helga Aguiar, Universidade de São Tomé e Príncipe;Felipe André Angst, Universidade Católica de Moçambique;José Augusto Guina, Universidade Politécnica – Campus de Nampula;Maria Raquel Vaz Patrício, Universidade Politécnica de Bragança;Rui Alexandre Martins Levy, Associação de Business Angels de Cabo Verde;Yuri Miguel Macedo, Universidade Federal da Bahia.LocalA CIETIA’27 realizar-se-á na Universidade Politécnica de Moçambique, em Maputo, Moçambique, entre os dias 14 e 16 de abril de 2027.O evento decorrerá em formato híbrido, permitindo a participação presencial e postings.conferenceName: Cognition: Interdisciplinary Foundations, Models and Applications
postings.conferenceText: Call for Papers – CIFMA 2026-----------------------------8th International Workshop on Cognition: Interdisciplinary Foundations, Models and Applications24 November 2026, Malta (Co-located with SEFM 2026)Background and ObjectivesCognition encompasses a wide range of intellectual functions and processes such as attention, memory, reasoning, problem solving, decision making, and language comprehension and production. Although rooted in psychology, the study of cognition now spans a wide array of disciplines, driven by the increasing complexity of human interaction with technological systems, virtual environments, and intelligent machines.CIFMA 2026 (https://cifma.github.io/) aims to provide a collaborative forum for researchers and practitioners from academia, industry, and research institutions who are interested in the foundations and applications of cognition. The workshop encourages interdisciplinary dialogue and concrete collaborations between fields such as computer science, logic, neuroscience, linguistics, cognitive robotics, philosophy, and more.The workshop specifically promotes the use of formal methods as a unifying approach to model and analyze cognitive systems and processes, extending well beyond their traditional use in software engineering.Contributions to the workshop cover the areas of education, research and technology, either in general or with a focus on formal methods. Topics are organized in possibly overlapping categories and include, but are not restricted to:Interdisciplinary Foundations of Cognition:- philosophy of cognition- human memory and memory processes- attention- perception, visual cognition and situated cognition- cognitive models and architectures- languages for cognitive science- social cognition- philosophy of modelling and simulation- philosophy of human-machine interactionCognitive Robotics:- autonomous knowledge acquisition- motor babbling- learning by imitation- cognitive architectures for robotics- biorobotics and biologically-inspired roboticsCognitive Linguistics:- cognitive approaches to grammar- cognitive and conceptual semantics- cognitive phonology- dynamical models of language acquisition- computational models of metaphor and language acquisition- corpus linguistics and conversational dataCognitive Learning:- learning theories- cognitive development- problem solving- metacognitionCognitive Neuroscience and Medicine:- biomedical signal and image processing- biomedical sensors and wearable systems- brain-computer interfaces and neural prostheses- brain mapping- neural and rehabilitation engineeringLogics and their application to:- human-computer interaction- human behaviour- human reasoning and problem solving- visual reasoning- human-robot interaction- linguistics- risk modelling in cognitionCognitive Computing:- artificial neural networks- human behaviour- cognitive analytics- human cognitive augmentation- cognitive computing hardware- AI cognitive systemsCognition and Software Engineering:- integration of cognitive models and cognitive architectures within the software design and verification process- cognitive aspects in cyber-physical systems and their verification- socio-technical systems- cognitive aspects in safety analysis and verification of safety-critical systems- cognitive security- cognition hackingCognition and Formal Methods:- formal frameworks for trust reasoning- formal methods for the modeling and analysis of robotic systems- formal methods for the modeling and analysis of human behaviour- formal methods for the modeling and analysis of human interaction with computers and robots- application of formal methods to cognitive psychology- formal frameworks for trust reasoningSubmission CategoriesWe welcome original, unpublished contributions in the following categories:- Research papers: novel results with formal analysis and discussion- Position papers: provocative and innovative ideas or frameworks- Case Study papers: real-world applications and lessons learned- Tool papers: description and evaluation of tools or componentsPlease indicate the paper category clearly in the EasyChair submission abstract (e.g., "This Research paper...")Submission GuidelinesRegular papers: 12–15 pages (LNCS format, references excluded); 12–16 pages for final post-proceedingsShort papers: 6–8 pages; 6–9 pages for final post-proceedingsPresentations: extended abstracts (up to 4 pages), included in pre-proceedings onlyAll submissions must be in English and formatted using the LNCS templates available at:LNCS postings.conferenceName: Fourth International Conference of Applied Industrial Engineering: Technology and Innovation for the Challenges of Green Engineering
postings.conferenceText: Topics: technological innovation and digital transformation clean energy and environmental governance education and knowledge transferThe 4th International Conference on Applied Industrial Engineering focuses on the key role of technology and innovation in addressing the challenges of green engineering, promoting sustainable development through efficient and responsible processes. From an industrial engineering perspective, the use of emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence, data analytics, automation, and sustainable energy systems enables the optimization of production, reduces environmental impact, and strengthens competitiveness. This approach drives the transition to circular economies, renewable energy, and strategic environmental management, integrating economic growth, social responsibility, and environmental sustainability as the foundation for the future of industry and society.Shipping GuidelinesAll submissions must be original and must not have been submitted simultaneously to another journal or conference.The topics are related to those described below:1. Technological innovation and digital transformation for sustainability.Application of Artificial Intelligence and Big Data in the optimization of sustainable processes.Industry 4.0 and intelligent automation for energy efficiency and waste reduction.Digital transformation in organizations: sustainable business models and circular economy.2. Clean energy and environmental governance.Integration of renewable energies (solar, wind, biomass) into industrial production systems.Public policies and regulatory frameworks for environmental management and sustainable development.Environmental impact assessment and climate change mitigation strategies in industry.3. Education and knowledge transfer for green engineering.Innovation in educational methodologies for training in sustainable engineering.Collaborations between universities and industry for the transfer of ecological technology and knowledge.Development of professional skills in sustainability and environmental responsibility.Detailed guidelines for authors preparing contributions can be found on the conference page at https://ciia.ug.edu.ec/instructions-for-authors-2026/The deadline for submitting papers is August 15, 2026, using the EasyChair article submission system (you will find the link at the top of the page).Decisions regarding acceptance or rejection will be communicated between July 31 and August 31, 2026.CommitteesChair of the Program CommitteeDoctor of Philosophy. postings.conferenceName: IX Congreso Internacional de Ingeniería de Sistemas / 9th International Conference on Systems Engineering
postings.conferenceText: Topics: data science computer science software engineering information systemsThe 9th International Conference on Systems Engineering (CIIS 2026) offers a unique platform for academic and practical dialogue on topics related to data science and artificial intelligence. Therefore, we invite researchers, professionals, and students to submit original research papers that contribute to the advancement of computer science, systems engineering, informatics, and related fields.Accepted papers presented at the conference will be published in the ACM International Conference Proceedings Series (ICPS), under the open access model, in the ACM Digital Library. The proceedings will be submitted to Scopus for consideration in accordance with its editorial criteria. The previous edition of this conference (CIIS 2025) was published in ACM ICPS, and its proceedings are indexed in Scopus. You can find it available in ACM DL and Scopus. Important DatesPaper Submission Deadline: June 30, 2026 July 13, 2026Notification of Acceptance and Review Committee Feedback: August 10, 2026Final Paper Submission Deadline: August 31, 2026TopicsManuscript Review Process1. Ensuring the integrity and confidentiality of the peer review processCIIS 2026 strictly adheres to the ACM Policy on Authorship and the Committee on Publication Ethics (COPE) guidelines for good publication practice. Any form of misconduct, including plagiarism or the improper use of third-party sources, will result in the immediate rejection of the manuscript. All individuals involved in the review process must declare any conflicts of interest and maintain the confidentiality of the manuscripts under evaluation. Under no circumstances may manuscripts or their content be shared outside the peer review process.2. Similarity report reviewThe chair, co-chair, and the Program Committee will review the similarity report to verify compliance with copyright laws, ethical standards, and the alignment of the manuscript with the thematic focus and main topics of the conference. Manuscripts with excessive similarity, inappropriate use of sources, or lack of alignment with the conference theme will be rejected.3. Assignment of manuscripts for reviewOnce approved for review, the manuscript will be assigned to members of the program committee or external experts specialized in the subject area. Each submission will be subject to a double-blind review by two independent reviewers, who will provide detailed comments and classify the manuscript as follows:Accepted without changes or with minor revisions.Conditionally accepted, but requiring major revisions based on the reviewers comments. The revised manuscript must be reviewed a second time for final approval.Rejected due to limited contributions or other concerns raised by the reviewers.4. Final decisionThe final decision on manuscript acceptance will be made by the program directors and conference chairs to ensure impartiality and academic quality.Instructions for AuthorsThe program only accepts papers written in English.CIIS 2026 follows the guidelines of the ACM Production System (TAPS) for manuscript preparation. Authors must use the official ACM templates (available in LaTeX and Word).Papers must be between 10 and 14 pages in ACM style, including the main content and references, and must be submitted in PDF format.Papers must preserve author anonymity; therefore, all identifiable information must be removed from both the text and the metadata.Papers must be original, innovative, and unpublished. In addition, they must not be simultaneously under review by other journals or academic conferences.Authors will be notified of the Review Committee's decision by the specified datePaper Publication and IndexingAccepted papers presented at the conference will be published in theACM International Conference Proceedings Series (ICPS)under the open access model, in the ACM Digital Library. The proceedings will be submitted to Scopus for consideration in accordance with its editorial criteria.The previous edition of this conference (CIIS 2025) was published in ACM ICPS, and its proceedings are indexed in Scopus.They are available at ACM DL and Scopus.The publication process will follow the workflow established by the ACM Production System (TAPS). Copyright for accepted papers will likewise be managed through the ACM e-Rights system.All accepted papers will be published in open access. Article processing charges (APC) will be covered by the conference; therefore, authors will not be required to make any payment for publication.For inclusion in the proceedings, at least one author of each paper must register for the conference and deliver the corresponding presentation, either onsite or virtually. Please refer to the conference registration section for further information.The Organizing Committee may invite promising submissions not selected for publication in ACM ICPS to be presented in poster format during the conference. These works may also be considered for the submission of an extended version for possible publication in a special section of Interfases (ISSN 1993-4912), a journal indexed in Redalyc, CrossRef, postings.conferenceName: CIKI–ICKM–GFIC Triple Conference 2026
postings.conferenceText: Topics: knowledge management knowledge engineering intellectual capital artificial intelligence The Next Horizon: Integrating AI, Knowledge, Innovation and Talent for Sustainable Global DevelopmentThe CIKI–ICKM–GFIC Triple Conference 2026 is a premier international event that brings together leading academics, researchers, professionals, and organizational leaders at the forefront of knowledge management, intellectual capital, innovation, artificial intelligence, and sustainability.Designed to foster high-level dialogue and meaningful exchange, the conference offers a dynamic format that combines scientific rigor with active participation, enabling direct interaction between research and practice. It is a space where ideas are not only presented, but challenged, connected, and transformed into actionable insights.This unique gathering is the result of a strategic collaboration between three globally recognized academic communities: CIKI, ICKM, and GFIC. The 2026 edition will be hosted by the Universidad de Santiago de Chile.CIKI–ICKM–GFIC 2026 offers a unique opportunity to understand the defining issues of the 21st century through the voices of those leading them—researchers, industry leaders, policymakers, and entrepreneurs—across diverse sectors and disciplines. SUBMISSION TYPESINDUSTRIAL/INNOVATION CASE STUDY (IN-PERSON/ONLINE): Seeks to share practical experiences, lessons learned, and solutions applied in real industrial, business, or public contexts. Cases of innovations applied in companies and the public sector are especially welcome. 200-300 words that will cover the main idea of the case.FULL PAPER (IN-PERSON/ONLINE): Must present original and significant contributions to scientific knowledge, validated through rigorous methods. Documents must contain between 4000-6000 words. Best papers will be considered for publication in the journals associated with the conference.POSTER (IN-PERSON ONLY): Seeks to highlight ideas and research proposals in the initial stages, ongoing research, and promising preliminary results. Contributions with academic standards are expected.

postings.conferenceName: “Human-Centered STEM Ecosystems and AI-Driven Technological Disruptions: Rethinking Engineering, Higher Education and Schooling in an Era of Uncertainty“
postings.conferenceText: Topics: emerging technologies in education innovative pedagogies and didactics stem ecosystems and educational policies humanistic and ethical dimensionsThe 8th Edition of the International Conference EVALSUP (French acronym for “Evaluation in HigherEducation”) and the 23th Edition of the CIMQUSEF (the International Conference on the Quality ofEducation and Training) are merged to converge into a single international conference that unites synergiesand optimizes resources to provide a platform for diverse stakeholders (academics, practitioners,policymakers, and organizations) to explore reflection and to promote exchange on the subject of qualityin education in light of the unprecedented changes and growing challenges affecting education systemsacross countries around the world. This scientific event will be held in Rabat-Morocco, on 28-29 October2026, under the theme: ”Human-Centered STEM Ecosystems and AI-Driven Technological Disruptions:Rethinking Engineering, Higher Education and Schooling in an Era of Uncertainty“. Scope and Objectives Artificial intelligence and rapid technological innovation are profoundly reshaping educationsystems worldwide. In an era of uncertainty and complexity, STEM education must go beyondtechnical skills to embrace humanistic values, ethics, sustainability and social responsibility.The CIMQUSEF/EVALSUP 2026 Conference provides an international forum for researchers,educators, practitioners and policymakers to explore emerging paradigms in STEMecosystems, AI-driven innovation and engineering education. Submission Guidelines All papers must be original and not simultaneously submitted to another journal or conference. Proposals for papers may be oral presentations, round-tables or workshops. The abstract should describe the problem, objectives, methodology and main results of the proposal. List of Topics Topic 1 – Humanistic and Ethical Dimensions of STEM Education : Ethics, citizenship, social responsibility, STEAM approaches, sustainability. Topic 2 – STEM Ecosystems and Educational Policies : Governance, partnerships, institutional strategies, internationalization. Topic 3 – Innovative Pedagogies and Didactics in STEM : Interdisciplinary approaches, active learning, teacher education. Topic 4 – Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technologies in Education : Generative AI, learning analytics, VR/AR, digital learning resources. Topic 5 – Engineering Education in an Era of Uncertainty and AI Disruptions : Future engineering competencies, systems thinking, ethics, curriculum transformation. Topic 6 – Equity, Inclusion and Diversity in STEM : Gender equity, inclusive practices, access and student success. Topic 7 – Research, Innovation and Entrepreneurship in Education : Knowledge transfer, innovation culture, maker-spaces, entrepreneurship. Topic 8 – Quality Assurance, Assessment and Impact of STEM Programs : Learning assessment, quality assurance, accreditation, impact studies. Committees Program Committee Aaron Benavot, USA Alain Bouvier, France Jean-Marie De Ketele, Belgium Janet Lord, UK Baiba Rivza, Latvia Organizing committee Samir Belfkih, Morocco Abdelali Kaaouachi, Morocco Abdennasser Naji, Morocco Invited Speakers Najat Vallaud-Belkacem, France Frédéric Fovet, Canada Olli-Pekka Heinonen, Finland Mohammed Slassi, Morocco Juliette Torabian, Switzerland Publication Selected papers will be published in the indexed journal “The Journal of Quality in Education”. Venue The conference will be held in ENSAM- Rabat, Morocco. Contact All questions about submissions should be emailed to amaquen@amaquen.org

postings.conferenceText: Topics: signal processing algorithm image analysis computerThe 2026 International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Multimodal Signal Processing (CIMSP 2026), scheduled for the 21-23th of August 2026. Hosted by Zhejiang University-University of illinois at Urbana-Champaign lnstitute (ZJUl), co-hosted by Information Technology Centre of Sindh Agriculture University Tandojam, University of Technology and Arts (ATA), and Robotics Society of Singapore. The conference in Xi'an, China, brings together researchers, educators, and industry leaders to explore the latest advancements in Intelligent Computing, Multimodal Singal Processing and related fields. Join us for insightful discussions, groundbreaking research, and collaborative networking opportunities aimed at driving innovation and sustainable solutions in these fields. We hope you will join us in Xi’an, China for CIMSP 2026. Submission Guidelines Submit your full paper to cimsp@outlook.com with "Paper Submission + TEL", or add the following number to contact the conference secretary. postings.conferenceName: The 24th International Conference on Computer and Information Technology
postings.conferenceText: CIT-2026 is the 24th edition of the highly successful International Conference on Computer and Information Technology. The goal of the conference is to provide a forum for scientists, engineers and researchers to discuss and exchange novel ideas, results, experiences and work-in-process on all aspects of computer and information technology. CIT has become a major platform for researchers and industry practitioners from different fields of computer and information technology. Each year, CIT attendees appreciate and benefit from multidisciplinary exchanges in computer and information technology. In previous years, CIT has attracted many high-quality research papers spanning over the various aspects of information technology, computing science and computer engineering. These papers highlight foundational work that strives to push beyond the limits of existing computer technologies, including experimental efforts, innovative systems, and investigations that identify weaknesses in existing IT services.CIT-2026 will be hosted in Exeter, the capital city of Devon and provides the county with a central base for education, medicine, religion, commerce and culture. The city is also home to the magnificent Exeter Cathedral, which dates back to Norman times. Exeter is also ideally placed to base a trip to branch out visiting places such as the famous Dartmoor National Park and the unspoilt beaches of the North and South Devon coastlines.Prospective authors are invited to submit their papers to CIT-2026. All accepted papers will be submitted to IEEE Xplore and will be submitted for indexing by Engineering Index (EI). The authors of selected best papers will be invited post conference to extend their contributions for special issues of prestigious journals to be planned in conjunction with the conference. SCOPE AND TOPICS================Topics of interest include, but are not limited to:Track 1: Computer ScienceTrack 2: Information TechnologyTrack 3: Networking and CommunicationsTrack 4: Information Security PAPER SUBMISSION GUIDELINE==========================All papers need to be submitted electronically through the conference submission website (https://hpcn.exeter.ac.uk/cit/) with PDF format. The materials presented in the papers should not be published or under submission elsewhere. Each paper is limited to 8 pages (or 10 pages with an over-length charge) including figures and references using IEEE Computer Society Proceedings Manuscripts style (two columns, single-spaced, 10 fonts).Once accepted, the paper will be included into the conference proceedings published by Conference Publishing Services (submitted for indexing by EI). At least one of the authors of any accepted paper is requested to register the paper at the conference. IMPORTANT DATES=================Submission Deadline: 25 July 2026 (extended)Authors Notification: 30 August 2026Final Manuscript Due: 30 September 2026Registration Due: 30 September 2026Conference Date: 26-28 October 2026For more information, please visit the conference website:https://hpcn.exeter.ac.uk/cit2026

postings.conferenceText: Topics: digital governance & ai smart cities & urban resilience digital health & applied bioengineering bioeconomy & sustainable manufacturingThe International Conference on Science, Technology and Innovation for Society (CITIS), organized by the Universidad Politécnica Salesiana (UPS) in Guayaquil, has established itself as a regional benchmark since 2014. This annual event brings together world-class researchers and academics to share their latest investigations and visions on global challenges. CITIS 2026 invites researchers, academics, and professionals to submit original, high-quality papers presenting innovative research at the intersection of science, technology, and society. All submissions must be written in English and will undergo a rigorous double-blind peer-review process.Submission GuidelinesBefore submitting, authors must ensure their manuscripts strictly comply with the following technical guidelines:Format & Template: Papers must be formatted exclusively according to the Springer Lecture Notes in Networks and Systems (LNNS) templates (Word or LaTeX). Submissions in other formats (IEEE, ACM, etc.) will not be accepted.Page Length: Manuscripts must be full papers with a strict length of 12 to 15 pages (including all figures, tables, and references). Short papers (under 12 pages) or over-length submissions (exceeding 15 pages) will be automatically subject to desk rejection.Co-authorship Limit: To foster extensive collaborative and multidisciplinary research, a maximum of 6 authors per manuscript is permitted.Anonymity (Double-Blind Review): The uploaded PDF must NOT contain author names, affiliations, emails, or explicit acknowledgments that reveal identity. Authors must also ensure that metadata identifying the creators is removed from the file properties. All author details must only be entered in the EasyChair metadata fields.Language: The entire paper, including tables, figures, and captions, must be written in English. Papers that do not meet this requirement will be immediately rejected (desk rejection).Originality and thematic alignment: Content must be original and aligned with at least one conference theme. All submissions will undergo a plagiarism analysis before peer review.Self-citation: Papers in which more than 20% of the references correspond to authors of the same paper will be automatically rejected (desk rejection).Accuracy and quality of graphical elements: Verify the accuracy of citations, diagrams, maps, and tables. All figures and tables must be inserted in the appropriate places in the text, as high-resolution, print-quality images.Use of generative artificial intelligence: All papers must include an AI usage statement detailing its purpose and scope within the work. The authors assume full responsibility for all content in the paper.Submission: All submissions must be made electronically in PDF format via the EasyChair platform.Note: These guidelines override previous limitations. For template downloads and full compliance details, authors should cross-reference this submission portal with the official portal guidelines. https://citis.ups.edu.ec/call-for-papers/instructions-for-authors/Important DatesTo ensure a rigorous and timely review process, the organizing committee will strictly adhere to the following schedule (Hard Deadlines):Full Paper Submission Deadline: July 25, 2026Full Paper Submission Deadline (Extended): August 10, 2026Acceptance Notification: August 25, 2026Camera-Ready & Author Registration: August 30, 2026Conference Dates: October 28 – October 30, 2026Note: Due to numerous requests, the paper submission deadline has been extended to August 10, 2026. postings.conferenceName: Continual Learning in Medical Multimodal-Vision
postings.conferenceText: Topics: continual and lifelong learning clinician in the loop learning adaptive and context aware clinical workflow integration and deploymentCLiMeM is the inaugural workshop held in conjunction with MICCAI 2026, taking place in Abu Dhabi in October 2026. It focuses on enabling medical AI systems to learn continuously and safely as clinical environments evolve. CLiMeM aims to bridge continual learning and medical multimodal vision to develop robust, physician-in-the-loop, and adaptable clinical AI systems. Topics include, but are not limited to: 1. Continual and Lifelong Learning Lifelong, continual, incremental, and online learning methods Sequential and multitask learning in medical settings Benchmark datasets, evaluation protocols, and metrics Catastrophic forgetting mitigation strategies 2. Clinician-in-the-Loop Learning Human–AI collaboration and interactive supervision Reinforcement learning for clinical decision support Preference learning from clinician feedback Implicit feedback signals (e.g., gaze, interaction logs) Annotation efficiency and active learning Trustworthy and interpretable clinical AI systems 3. Adaptive and Context-Aware Inference Test-time adaptation and online domain generalization Memory- and retrieval-augmented models Context-aware and causal modeling Resource-constrained and real-time adaptation 4. Clinical Workflow Integration and Deployment Integration with PACS, EHR, RIS, and imaging workstations Deployment using platforms such as MONAI Label, OHIF, and 3D Slicer Continual learning infrastructure and model governance User-centred clinical system design Important Dates July 9th, 2026 (23:59 PDT)Paper submission deadline July 30th, 2026Author notification August 6th, 2026 (23:59 PDT)Camera-ready deadline TBAIn-person workshop @MICCAI 2026 (October 2026)

postings.conferenceName: Clinical-MIRF: Multimodal Information Retrieval and Fusion in Clinical Workflows
postings.conferenceText: Topics: multimodal fusion multimodal retrieval representation learning and modality alignment retrieval augmented generation for healthcareClinical workflows are increasingly information-intensive, requiring the joint interpretation of heterogeneous data sources, including medical images, electronic health records (EHRs), clinical notes, and biomedical knowledge. While these complementary sources provide a richer understanding of patient conditions, they also introduce significant challenges in information retrieval, integration, fusion, and clinical reasoning.Recent advances in multimodal foundation models, vision-language models, and retrieval-augmented generation have created new opportunities for AI-based clinical decision support. However, important challenges remain, including cross-modal retrieval, representation alignment, multimodal fusion, and the development of robust, fair, interpretable, and privacy-preserving systems for high-stakes clinical environments.The workshop Clinical-MIRF: Multimodal Information Retrieval and Fusion in Clinical Workflows addresses these challenges by positioning clinical AI as an information retrieval and knowledge integration problem. It aims to bring together researchers from information retrieval, knowledge management, multimodal learning, biomedical Natural Language Processing (NLP), medical imaging, EHR analytics, and clinical AI to discuss methods, datasets, evaluation protocols, and deployment challenges for multimodal clinical information systems.The main objectives of the workshop are:Establish multimodal retrieval and fusion for clinical workflows as an emerging research area.Foster collaboration across information retrieval, knowledge management, medical imaging, biomedical NLP, and clinical AI communities.Discuss challenges in retrieval, fusion, alignment, reasoning, evaluation, robustness, fairness, and privacy.Identify open datasets, benchmarks, evaluation protocols, and deployment barriers.Topics include, but are not limited to:Multimodal information retrieval and cross-modal searchRetrieval-augmented generation for healthcareRepresentation learning and modality alignmentVision-language and multimodal foundation modelsMultimodal fusion for clinical decision supportKnowledge graphs and clinical knowledge integrationExplainability, trustworthiness, robustness, and fairness in multimodal clinical LogicA.1 Mathematical LogicA.2 Philosophical LogicA.3 Computational Logic and Applications of LogicA.4 Historical Aspects of LogicA.5 Educational Aspects of LogicB. General Philosophy of ScienceB.1 MethodologyB.2 Formal Philosophy of Science and Formal EpistemologyB.3 Empirical and Experimental Philosophy of Science and TechnologyB.4 Metaphysical Issues in the Philosophy of Science and TechnologyB.5 Ethical, Social and Political Issues in the Philosophy of Science and TechnologyB.6 Historical Aspects in the Philosophy of Science and TechnologyB.7 Educational Aspects of Philosophy of Science and TechnologyC. Philosophical Issues of Particular DisciplinesC.1 Philosophy of the Formal Sciences (including Logic, Mathematics, Statistics)C.2 Philosophy of the Physical Sciences (including Physics, Chemistry, Earth Science, Climate Science)C.3 Philosophy of the Biological SciencesC.4 Philosophy of the Biomedical and Health SciencesC.5 Philosophy of the Cognitive and Behavioural SciencesC.6 Philosophy of Computing and ComputationC.7 Philosophy of the Humanities and the Social SciencesC.8 Philosophy of the Applied Sciences and TechnologyC.9 Philosophy of Emerging and Interdisciplinary SciencesThe language of the congress is English. Contributed papersSubmissions will be made through the EasyChair platform, which will be available in early August.Once the submission page is open, please submit an abstract of 500 words, including the references, prepared for anonymous review. Indicate to which congress section you submit the paper (tick the appropriate box). The allocated time for each contributed paper is 30 minutes, including discussion. Contributed symposiaSymposia are groups of talks on a common theme. Each symposium consists of four to twelve papers.In EasyChair (which will be available in early August), please make a submission for (a) the symposium as a whole; and (b) each paper in the symposium (so, for example, for a four-paper symposium, you should make a total of five submissions).(a) For the symposium as a whole, please provide an abstract with a general description of the format and the topic of the proposed symposium and its significance (up to 500 words), and suggest a symposium chair. If desired, it is acceptable for the symposium organiser to be the chair. Indicate to which congress section you submit the symposium (tick the appropriate box). After the abstract, please list the titles of the talks in the order they should appear at the conference. Please provide the symposium with an acronym, and write this acronym at the beginning of the title of the symposium (:). The acronym will be used by the Programme Committee to keep the individual submissions in a proposal together during reviewing and when creating the conference programme.(b) For each paper within a symposium, please submit a 500-word abstract (including references). Indicate to which congress section the symposium belongs (tick the appropriate box). Please write the acronym of the symposium at the beginning of the title of the talk (:). The acronym will be used by the Programme Committee to keep the individual submissions in a proposal together during reviewing and when creating the conference program.Note to symposium organisers: papers intended to be presented as parts of a symposium must be submitted by their respective authors. Symposium organisers should contact all symposium speakers in advance and make sure that they submit their abstracts by the submission deadline of 15 November 2026 (tentative). The symposium description is submitted by the symposium organiser by the same deadline. Please make sure that all parts of the submission are prepared for anonymous review and submitted to the same congress section (the same box is ticked in all of them). When submitting a symposium proposal, the EasyChair requires you to take the role of a “speaker“. This is for formal reasons only, and in no way precludes you from submitting a paper of your own (to that same symposium, to a different symposium, or a contributed paper). In this case, you will appear as a “speaker“ on 2 submissions, one of which must be the symposium proposal.Although the exact format of symposia is up to the symposium organizers, the allocated time for each symposium paper is 30 minutes. For instance, a symposium with 4 speakers is a 2 hour session (4 x 30 minutes). Note that if a symposium consists of more than 4 speakers, it might be split into two sessions due to coffee breaks in the programme. Registration requirementsThe corresponding author of each individual paper and of each symposium paper as well as the organiser of a symposium must be registered in advance of the Congress and present the paper in Kobe. Failure to register by the specified date may result in cancellation of the accepted paper and/or symposium.The following rules also apply for multiple presentations:(a) Every corresponding author is allowed to submit only one individual or symposium paper as a “speaker.” (Organising a symposium does not count as being a “speaker,” despite the labelling in EasyChair.)(b) Authors are permitted to be listed as non-corresponding co-authors of additional papers. postings.conferenceName: The 17th International Conference on Cloud Computing Technology and Science
postings.conferenceText: The 17th IEEE International Conference on Cloud Computing Technology and Science (CloudCom 2026) is the premier conference for researchers, engineers, and practitioners to present their latest research results, ideas, and applications in the areas of Cloud, Edge, and Fog computing. CloudCom 2026 aims to provide a high-quality forum for discussing the evolving ecosystem of cloud-native technologies, serverless architectures, and the integration of AI within distributed environments. Submission Guidelines All papers must be original and not simultaneously submitted to another journal or conference. The following paper categories are welcome: Full papers: Describing original, completed research that contributes to the state-of-the-art in Cloud Computing. Full papers should not exceed 8 pages (IEEE format), including figures, tables, and references. Short papers: Describing "work-in-progress" or preliminary results that show high promise but are not yet fully matured. Short papers should not exceed 4 pages. Posters/Demos: Describing innovative tools, prototypes, or visual representations of research concepts. These submissions should include a 2-page extended abstract. List of Topics Topic 1: Architecture and Virtualization (Hypervisors, Containers, Serverless, Microservices, and Software-Defined Infrastructure) Topic 2: Cloud Services and Applications (SaaS/PaaS/IaaS, Cloud-native apps, Big Data analytics, and E-commerce) Topic 3: Security, Privacy, and Trust (Identity management, data encryption in the cloud, regulatory compliance, and Zero Trust architectures) Topic 4: Edge, Fog, and Mobile Cloud (Cloud-to-Edge continuum, IoT integration, and low-latency distributed computing) Topic 5: Intelligence in the Cloud (AI/ML for cloud management, AIOps, and large-scale model training on cloud infrastructure) Topic 6: Sustainability and Green Cloud (Energy-efficient data centers, carbon-aware computing, and sustainable resource scheduling) Committees Program Committee Dr. Wissam Mallouli - Montimage Prof. Ana Cavalli - IMT-SudParis Edgardo montes de oca - ModelPlus Organizing committee Dr. Wissam Mallouli - Montimage Prof. Ana Cavalli - IMT-SudParis Edgardo montes de oca - ModelPlus Mahdi Karray - Montimage Luong Nguyen - Montimage Bastien Repaire - Montimage Venue Hotel ibis Paris Alésia Montparnasse 14ème 49 Rue des Plantes, 75014 Paris France Contact All questions about submissions should be emailed to wissam.mallouli@montimage.eu

postings.conferenceText: Topics: databases and information systems data science and artificial intelligence computer networks and security knowledge discovery and managementScopeThe Conference on Research in Computer Science and its Applications (CNRIA) is an international scientific conference that highlights new trends and advances in current topics in the field of computing and their applications for development. CNRIA is co-organized by the Senegalese Association of Researchers in Computer Science (ASCII) and the Ecole Polytechnique de Thiès (EPT).The main purpose of the CNRIA 2026 conference is to serve as a forum for researchers from academia, ICT industry and development actors to discuss recent advances and cutting-edge topics in the field of computer science and its applications. This conference also serves as a forum for exchanging ideas, proposing solutions, discussing research challenges and sharing experiences between researchers, professionals and development actors. CNRIA 2026 aims at promoting the popularization of the contributions of the regional scientific community in new cutting-edge research topics such as AI, IoT, Big Data, Cloud Computing, Security, SDN, etc.This 16th edition of CNRIA will be held on October 15 to 17, 2026 at the Ecole Polytechnique de Thiès, Senegal.Submission GuidelinesAll papers must be original and not simultaneously submitted to another journal or conference. The following paper categories are welcome:Full papers: The regular papers for oral presentation must not exceed 6 pages with IEEE double columns conference paper template (DOC, LATEX (Source , Biblio)). All submission should be strictly done anonymously with authors names and affiliations left blank.Demos : This demo track provides a unique platform for researchers, practitioners, startups, and industry players to demonstrate live systems, tools, prototypes, and applications that leverage emerging technologies. The demo proposal should not exceed 3 pages with IEEE double columns conference paper template. All submission should be strictly done anonymously with authors names and affiliations left blank.Tutorials : The Tutorial Track of CNRIA 2026 aims to offer participants an opportunity to gain in-depth knowledge and hands-on experience on emerging and established topics in Computer Science and its Applications. Tutorials are intended to complement the technical program by providing structured, pedagogical, and practice-oriented presentations delivered by recognized experts from academia and industry.This track welcomes proposals that present foundational concepts, state-of-the-art research advances, tools, platforms, methodologies, and real-world applications. Tutorials should be accessible to a broad audience, including graduate students, researchers, engineers, and practitioners, while also offering sufficient technical depth to benefit experienced participants.The Tutorial Track seeks to promote knowledge transfer, skill development, and community building, enabling attendees to better understand current technologies, explore emerging research directions, and apply computer science techniques to solve complex real-world problems. The tutorial proposal should not exceed 1 pages with IEEE double columns conference paper template. All submission should be strictly done anonymously with authors names and affiliations left blank.Early-stage research papers (Jeunes chercheurs) : The Early Stage Researcher (ESR) track of the CNRIA 2026 is a dedicated forum designed to foster the research vocation of Master 2 and PhD students. This session provides a privileged and supportive environment for researchers in the first years of their career to present their ongoing work, exchange innovative ideas, and receive constructive guidance from the scientific community.The primary goal of the ESR track is to bridge the gap between initial research ideas and confirmed scientific contributions. In contrast to the main conference tracks, this session focuses on:Work-in-Progress: Allowing participants to present preliminary results or research designs that are not yet sufficiently accomplished for a full paper.Constructive Feedback: Facilitating direct interaction between junior researchers and experienced Principal Investigators (PIs) to refine methodologies and research goals.Skill Development: Enhancing communication skills through the "My Research in 180 Seconds" (Flash Talk) format and poster presentations.Networking: Building interdisciplinary and international networks to encourage collaborative research across the Global South and beyond.This session is specially designed for:Master 2 students initiating their research path.PhD students (typically in their 1st to 4th year) who have not yet awarded their doctoral degree.Early-career researchers in industry or academia seeking feedback on new research directions.Prospective authors are invited to submit a short paper (up to 2 pages, with IEEE double columns conference paper template) highlighting the research context, problem statement, methodology, and preliminary results. All submission should be strictly done anonymously with authors names and affiliations left blank. postings.conferenceName: 14. Symposium Communications for Energy Systems
postings.conferenceText: ComForEn 2027Die ComForEn 2027 findet am 19. und 20. Jänner 2027 in Wien statt und wird gemeinschaftlich vom AIT Austrian Institute of Technology und dem OVE Österreichischer Verband für Elektrotechnik organisiert sowie von der Technologieplattform Smart Grids Austria unterstützt.Mit ihrer mittlerweile 14. Ausgabe blickt die ComForEn auf eine erfolgreiche Geschichte zurück und hat sich als eine der traditionsreichsten Fachveranstaltungen für Energiesysteme in Österreich etabliert. Der Tagungsort Wien bietet dabei als historisches Zentrum und zugleich moderner Innovationsknotenpunkt für Energietechnologien den idealen Rahmen, um gemeinsam mit Experten aus Wissenschaft und Wirtschaft die digitale Transformation der Energienetze voranzutreiben. Wir freuen uns darauf, Sie zu diesem etablierten Dialog persönlich vor Ort begrüßen zu dürfen: Die Präsenz in Wien ermöglicht es den Teilnehmern, in einer inspirierenden Atmosphäre Kontakte zu knüpfen, in den Pausen tiefgehende Diskussionen zu führen und das spannende Rahmenprogramm gemeinsam zu erleben.Intelligente Systemintegration: Flexibilitäten durch IKT skalierbar machenIm Zentrum steht die Frage, wie die wachsende Zahl an dezentralen Ressourcen durch moderne Informations- und Kommunikationstechnologien (IKT) effizient in das Gesamtsystem integriert werden kann. Die Konferenz bietet:Hochkarätige Vorträge: Ein Mix aus geladenen Keynotes und peer-reviewed Fachbeiträgen.Best Practices: Einblicke in die praktische Umsetzung von Netzbetreibern, Lieferanten und der Industrie.Persönliches Networking: Ein spannendes Rahmenprogramm, das viel Zeit für den direkten Austausch und neue Kooperationen bietet.Call for PapersDie Transformation zu einem klimaneutralen Energiesystem erfordert die Integration neuer Technologien über verschiedene Sektoren hinweg. Interoperabilität und intelligente IKT-Lösungen sind dabei entscheidende Erfolgsfaktoren für die Stabilität unserer Netze.Wir laden Forscherinnen, Entwickler und Praktiker herzlich ein, ihre Beiträge zu den folgenden Schwerpunkten einzureichen:Disruptive Flexibilitäten: Integration von Rechenzentren (Data Centers) als aktive Systemkomponenten.Sektor-Kopplung & Elektrifizierung: Nutzung der Flexibilitätspotenziale aus dem Wärme- und Mobilitätssektor.Digitale Kundenschnittstelle: Erfahrungen und Herausforderungen bei der Umsetzung in Österreich.KI & Automatisierung: Einsatz künstlicher Intelligenz für das Management lokaler Energiegemeinschaften und virtueller Kraftwerke.Standardisierung & Protokolle: Fortschritte bei der DSO-Retailer-Kommunikation und TSO-DSO-Interaktion.Lessons Learned: Erfolgsgeschichten und Best Practices aus der praktischen Umsetzung.Einreichung und PublikationWir freuen uns auf spannende Beiträge aus der Forschung sowie Best Practices aus der praktischen Umsetzung – sowohl aus Sicht der Wissenschaft als auch aus der Perspektive von Netzbetreibern, Lieferanten und der Industrie.Review: Alle eingereichten Beiträge werden einem Peer-Review-Verfahren unterzogen.Tagungsband: Akzeptierte Beiträge werden im offiziellen ComForEn-Tagungsband veröffentlicht. Dieser wird, wie in den Vorjahren, mit einer ISBN-Nummer versehen und online frei verfügbar sein, um eine breite Sichtbarkeit der Ergebnisse zu gewährleistenSprache: Die Konferenzsprache ist Deutsch, Paper können in Deutsch oder Englisch verfasst werden. Templates stehen unter www.comforen.org zur Verfügung.Archiv & Impressionen: Informationen über vorherige Ausgaben der Konferenz (einschließlich der Tagungsbände und Fotogalerien) können auf der Homepage www.comforen.org eingesehen werden.Wichtige TermineDeadline zur Einreichung der Beiträge: 25.09.2026Annahmebestätigung: 30.10.2026Konferenztermin: 19.-20.01.2027Werden Sie Teil der ComForEn 2027 und gestalten Sie die digitale Energiezukunft aktiv mit! Weitere Informationen und Templates finden Sie unter www.comforen.org.

postings.conferenceName: Workshop on Computational Methods in the Humanities 2026
postings.conferenceText: CALL FOR PAPERS 3rd workshop on Computational Methods in the Humanities (COMHUM 2026) September 9–10, 2026 — University of Lausanne, Switzerland Special track: computation and video games Without doubt, the digital has become an integral part of our everyday experience, whether it is due to our use of digital devices, the ever-increasing amounts of data collected and processed by said devices, or the prevalence of LLMs and AI agents in most websites or softwares. Academia and the humanities have never been more digital, which pushes digital humanities to frontiers beyond computational approaches to humanities or the application of humanities research methods to the digital. In this context, the COMHUM workshop series positions itself as an international forum primarily devoted to the following research questions: (1) which formal or computational approaches can help address the particular challenges posed by the growing presence of the digital in humanities, e.g., digital artifacts, software, LLMs, and computer-generated data? In these cases and beyond, (2) which methods are most appropriate to tackle the challenges posed by humanities research and how can they be applied to concrete research questions? The first day will be devoted to the specific topic of computation and video games. This topic explores computational methods for analyzing video games as well as humanities approaches to computation in video games. It has a number of ramifications in a variety of disciplines, including software studies, critical code studies, literary analysis, digital humanities, and game studies. It is of particular interest for a number of research initiatives at UNIL and in neighboring institutions. COMHUM 2026 will be a perfect opportunity to bring together researchers from various communities studying video games using computational approaches or studying computation in video games, to review the state of the art in this domain and to outline its future developments. In the spirit of the previous editions of the COMHUM workshop, the second day will be open to submissions on any topic pertaining to theoretical or applied research on computational methods for humanities research broadly conceived. The program will consist of invited and contributed talks. The official language of the workshop is English. Contributions can be submitted in English or French. Topics The topics of the workshop are divided into two tracks. The special track focuses on formal and computational approaches to video games as digital artifacts as well as humanities approaches to computation in video games. This can include research related to the development and use of computational methods for video game analysis, including reverse engineering, decompiling and data collection, or analysis of computation and the emergence of code in video games, including their influence on narrative, gameplay and design. Topics in the special track include, but are not limited to: Methods for data extraction in video games (e.g. telemetry, assets, models, code) Computational methods for video game analysis (including spatial, representational and narrative aspects) Analyses of intersection of computational approaches and the study of video games Humanities approaches to computation of video games (including software) In addition, an open track welcomes submissions on formal and computational aspects related to the development and use of computational methods in the humanities in general (with a particular interest for the disciplines represented in the Faculty of Arts of UNIL, such as literature, linguistics, history, history of art, cinema studies, archaeology or philosophy). Topics in the open track include, but are not limited to: Theoretical issues of formal modeling in the humanities Knowledge representation in the humanities Data structures addressing specific problems in the humanities (including text and markup) Computational methods in the humanities (e.g., for language and literary studies, historical studies, or multimodal data) Applications of computer vision, image analysis and spatial analysis in the humanities Submissions We invite researchers to submit abstracts of 500 to 1000 words (excluding references). Abstracts will be reviewed double-blind by the members of the program committee, and all submissions will receive at least two independent reviews. Abstracts submitted at review stage must not contain the authors’ names, affiliations, or any information that may disclose the authors’ identity. Authors of accepted abstracts will be invited to present their research at the workshop as a talk, and the abstracts will be published in the book of abstracts of the workshop. The abstracts must use the ACL format (LaTeX, Word). Abstracts must be submitted electronically in PDF format. For abstract submissions we use EasyChair. Authors of accepted contributions can be invited, after the conference, to submit a full paper version (6–16 pages), which, after peer-review, will be published in an open-access, electronic conference volume endowed with persistent identifiers (to be confirmed soon). postings.conferenceName: The 2nd International Workshop on Socio-technical Approaches to Content Moderation and Platform Governance
postings.conferenceLocation: Salt Lake City, Utah, United States
postings.conferenceText: Topics: content moderation platform governance human computer interaction artificial intelligenceToday, online platforms navigate a growing range of harms, including misinformation, hate speech, harassment, exploitative material, and coordinated manipulation. Content moderation is an essential yet increasingly complex component of how these platforms maintain safe, trustworthy, and inclusive online environments. The rapid advancement of technologies such as generative AI, evolving platform infrastructures, and decentralized moderation systems further complicates this landscape, introducing new forms of misbehavior while also creating new opportunities for moderation research and practice. At the same time, content moderation extends well beyond automated detection: it involves defining and interpreting community guidelines, designing and evaluating interventions, supporting moderators and affected users, and balancing competing values such as safety, transparency, privacy, and freedom of expression. Addressing these challenges requires a holistic, multidisciplinary perspective that bridges socio-technical approaches, human-centered design, governance, ethics, law, and regulation.This workshop aims to foster a comprehensive dialogue on content moderation and platform governance, engaging researchers and practitioners from diverse backgrounds, including CSCW, HCI, social computing, computational social science, law, communication, trust and safety, and related fields. Building on the strong engagement and interdisciplinary discussions of the first COMPASS workshop held at ICWSM 2025, this second edition will advance understanding, spark collaborations, and drive innovation across the full spectrum of moderation challenges, from community governance and intervention design to evaluation, transparency, and accountability.Given CSCW’s longstanding commitment to understanding complex socio-technical systems and the interplay between technology and society, COMPASS will provide an ideal venue for meaningful discussion, cross-disciplinary exchange, and actionable insights into the moderation and governance challenges shaping contemporary online ecosystems.Submission GuidelinesWe welcome the following types of submissions:Research papers (up to 10 pages including references, but excluding appendices) presenting full-fledged, mature scientific work. This can either be novel or already submitted/published at another venue.Resource papers (up to 10 pages including references, but excluding appendices) presenting datasets, applications, softwares, or demos. These can either be novel or already submitted/published at another venue.Work-in-progress papers (up to 5 pages including references, but excluding appendices) presenting preliminary results.Vision and position papers (up to 5 pages including references and appendices) presenting new ideas.List of TopicsThe workshop welcomes contributions spanning topics such as:Community guidelines and governance: Design, evolution, and impact of platform policies, and their alignment with community norms and regulatory frameworks.Moderation interventions and downstream effects: Design and evaluation of interventions (e.g., removals, warnings, visibility modifications), including causal inference and downstream effects.Metrics and evaluation: Measures of moderation effectiveness, platform health, and societal impact.Human-centered moderation: Interactions between human moderators, users, and automated systems; psychological and experiential dimensions.Cross-cultural and societal dimensions of moderation: Cross-cultural differences, inclusivity, and the role of diverse communities in shaping moderation practices.Legal and regulatory implications: Impacts of frameworks such as the DSA and AI Act on platform governance and accountability.Ethics and values: Trade-offs between safety, privacy, autonomy, and freedom of expression.Data and transparency: Access to moderation data, auditing practices, and reproducibility challenges.Decentralized and participatory moderation: Community-driven and distributed approaches to moderation and governance.Emerging technologies: Moderation challenges related to generative AI, LLM-powered moderation interventions, live and real-time content, and new platform modalities.Moderation challenges involving vulnerable or high-profile populations: Unique moderation concerns in the context of special groups, such as politicians, activists, journalists, and children.CommitteesProgram CommitteeThales Bertaglia, Maastricht University, NetherlandsJie Cai, Tsinghua University, ChinaLorenzo Cima, IIT-CNR, ItalyJordi Guillem Condom Tibau, University of Pisa & IIT-CNR, ItalyDaria Dergacheva, University of Bremen, GermanyRoberto Di Pietro, KAUST, Saudi ArabiaRobert Gorwa, WZB Berlin Social Science Center, GermanyAnna Monreale, University of Pisa, ItalyAlice Qian, Carnegie Mellon University, USAFabrizio Silvestri, "La Sapienza" University of Rome, ItalyBenedetta Tessa, University of Pisa & IIT-CNR, Italy(more to be announced soon)Organizing CommitteeLocal OrganizersShagun Jhaver, Rutgers University, USASanjay Kairam, OpenAI, USAKoustuv Saha, University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, USARemote OrganizersRobyn Caplan, Duke University, USAStefano Cresci, IIT-CNR, ItalyCatalina Goanta, University of Utrecht, NetherlandsSavvas Zannettou, TU Delft, NetherlandsContactAll questions about submissions should be emailed to stefano.cresci@iit.cnr.it.

La sociedad 5.0, en puerta, permitirá la creación de Ecosistemas mediante la integración de Inteligencia Artificial, Big Data, Internet de las Cosas - IoT, Robótica y la red 5G, permitiendo potencializar trabajos de investigación bajo metodologías, modelos matemáticos y técnicas.Aunado a este entorno la pandemia por el COVID-19 ha desatado una serie de hipótesis, análisis y procesamiento de datos, así como innovaciones en modelos para ayudar a comprender el comportamiento del virus y pronosticar los escenarios probables a enfrentar, es así que muchos grupos de investigación en todo el mundo están enfocados en este gran suceso que enfrenta la humanidad y donde nuestro país no es la excepción, por ello en todas las disciplinas se están realizando esfuerzos acelerados en esta carrera contra el tiempo.Ante este panorama es preciso redoblar esfuerzos para continuar generando y aplicando conocimientos encausados en mejorar las condiciones de vida, por ello el CONACIC2026 por DECIMOSEXTO año consecutivo, será el escenario donde investigadores, docentes, profesionales y público en general, preocupados por el avance y aplicación de las Ciencias Computacionales disfruten de un ambiente de plena discertación, intercambio y análisis en torno a ésta apasionante y estratégica área del conocimiento.ContribucionesEl Comité Organizador del VIII Congreso Internacional y XVI Congreso Nacional de Ciencias de la Computación (CONACIC 2026), invita a la comunidad científica y académica a enviar sus trabajos para participar en este foro en la modalidad de presentación oral (máximo 10 hojas). postings.conferenceName: VIII Congreso Internacional, XVI Congreso Nacional de Ciencias de la Computación
postings.conferenceText: Topics: artificial intelligence data science robotics healthEl comienzo de este nuevo siglo vino acompañado de grandes desarrollos, cambios y desafíos que inciden en todos los aspectos de la vida cotidiana: trabajo, economía, salud, etc. La investigación acompañada del surgimiento de nuevas tecnologías provee propuestas que permiten enfrentar estos retos y resolver problemas actuales. La sociedad 5.0, en puerta, permitirá la creación de Ecosistemas mediante la integración de Inteligencia Artificial, Big Data, Internet de las Cosas - IoT, Robótica y la red 5G, permitiendo potencializar trabajos de investigación bajo metodologías, modelos matemáticos y técnicas.Aunado a este entorno la pandemia por el COVID-19 ha desatado una serie de hipótesis, análisis y procesamiento de datos, así como innovaciones en modelos para ayudar a comprender el comportamiento del virus y pronosticar los escenarios probables a enfrentar, es así que muchos grupos de investigación en todo el mundo están enfocados en este gran suceso que enfrenta la humanidad y donde nuestro país no es la excepción, por ello en todas las disciplinas se están realizando esfuerzos acelerados en esta carrera contra el tiempo.Ante este panorama es preciso redoblar esfuerzos para continuar generando y aplicando conocimientos encausados en mejorar las condiciones de vida, por ello el CONACIC2026 por DECIMOSEXTO año consecutivo, será el escenario donde investigadores, docentes, profesionales y público en general, preocupados por el avance y aplicación de las Ciencias Computacionales disfruten de un ambiente de plena discertación, intercambio y análisis en torno a ésta apasionante y estratégica área del conocimiento.ContribucionesEl Comité Organizador del VIII Congreso Internacional y XVI Congreso Nacional de Ciencias de la Computación (CONACIC 2026), invita a la comunidad científica y académica a enviar sus trabajos para participar en este foro en la modalidad de presentación oral (máximo 10 hojas). Los trabajos aceptados y presentados serán publicados como:Capítulos de libro con ISBN ó,Artículo en la revista Abstraction and Application de la Facultad de Matemáticas, Universidad Autónoma de Yucatán con ISSN: 2007-2635.Los autores cuyos trabajos sean publicados en Abstraction and Application, serán invitados a someter una versión extendida de la versión publicada considerando que difiera al menos un 40% en su contenido teórico, resultados experimentales y referencias bibliográficas, para una nueva revisión por pares y su eventual publicación en las revistas JCR, International Journal Of Combinatorial Optimization Problems And Informatics o Computación y Sistemas.TópicosSon bienvenidos todos los trabajos relacionados con la práctica docente, desarrollo de aplicaciones e investigación sobre los siguientes temas, pero no restringido a ellos:Big DataComputación CuánticaCloud ComputingComputación y SociedadCómputo CientíficoCiberSeguridadCiencia de DatosIngeniería de SoftwareInteligencia ArtificialIoTRealidad Virtual y AumentadaRobóticaSistemas DistribuidosSistemas EmbebidosTIC's en la EducaciónTópico Especial de "Investigación y Educación para la Salud"Atenta invitación a someter sus trabajos a revisión por pares para su inclusión en el Tópico Especial de Investigación y Educación para la Salud. Fechas importantesLanzamiento de convocatoria: 23 de febreroLímite para envío de trabajos: 15 de junio 13 de julio NUEVA FECHANotificación de aceptación o rechazo: 6 de julio 3 de agosto NUEVA FECHALímite para envío de la versión final: 6 de agosto 31 de agosto NUEVA FECHAEnvío de ArtículosSon bienvenidos todos los artículos científicos que cumplan con los siguientes requerimientos:Longitud máxima 10 hojas.Escrito en inglés o español.Formato "PLANTILLA"La revisión de los trabajos será mediante "Doble Ciego", por lo cual se solicita no incluir los autores en la primera version.Plataforma de envío de artículos Easychair (Exclusivamente por este medio)SedeFacultad de Ciencias de la Computación, Benemérita Universidad Autónoma de Puebla.EVENTO EN MODALIDAD VIRTUAL.Comité OrganizadorComité Organizador GeneralDr. Juan Humberto Sossa Azuela, Coordinador Honorario, Centro de Investigación en Computación, Instituto Politécnico Naicional.Dr. Gustavo Trinidad Rubín Linares, Coordinador General, Facultad de Ciencias de la Computación, Benemérita Universidad Autónoma Puebla.Comité OrganizadorDra. postings.conferenceName: 36° Congreso Nacional de Geoquímica
postings.conferenceText: Topics: geochemistry geology environmental chemistry earth sciencesCONAGEQ 2026El Congreso Nacional de Geoquímica (CONAGEQ) es el encuentro académico más importante en México especializado en el estudio de la química de la Tierra y sus aplicaciones. Es organizado anualmente por el Instituto Nacional de Geoquímica (INAGEQ A. C.), la asociación científica que agrupa a investigadoras(es), científicas(os), profesionistas y estudiantes del área de Geoquímica y disciplinas afines a las Ciencias de la Tierra en México.ObjetivoEl congreso tiene como propósito generar un espacio de intercambio de conocimientos y experiencias para promover soluciones a problemas vinculados con la química de sistemas naturales, así como difundir los logros científicos alcanzados y fortalecer la formación de nuevas vocaciones científicas en el país.ActividadesEl programa incluye cursos precongreso, conferencias magistrales, sesiones técnicas (con presentaciones orales y carteles) y un viaje de campo.TemáticasEn este congreso las sesiones técnicas se organizan conforme a los ejes generales y transversales del Plan Nacional de Desarrollo 20245-2030, integrando la investigación geoquímica de frontera con los principios de justicia social, igualdad sustantiva, innovación tecnológica, educación y sostenibilidad ambiental. Las áreas temáticas incluidas en este congreso corresponden a las desarrolladas históricamente por la comunidad del INAGEQ y solo han sido reorganizadas en el marco del Plan Nacional de Desarrollo, con la finalidad de fortalecer la pertinencia social de la ciencia, así como contribuir a la formación de especialistas comprometidos/as con la atención de los principales retos ambientales y territoriales del país y del mundo.Sesión Técnica General 1. Gobernanza con justicia y participación ciudadanaEste eje agrupa las contribuciones científicas orientadas a la toma de decisiones públicas, a la reducción de las desigualdades socioambientales y a la construcción de una gobernanza ambiental participativa.STG1-01. Gobernanza ambiental y políticas públicasSTG1-02. Ciencia participativa y monitoreo comunitarioSTG1-03. Riesgo ambiental y poblaciones vulnerablesSTG1-04. Investigaciones en otros campos de la geoquímicaSesión Técnica General 2. Desarrollo con bienestar y humanismoEste eje integra la geoquímica y las ciencias de la Tierra en la protección de la salud, el bienestar humano y la formación de capacidades científicas.STG2-01. Biogeoquímica en sistemas suelo–agua–biotaSTG2-02. Química atmosféricaSTG2-03. Geoquímica ambiental y saludSTG2-04. Procesos de especiación, movilidad y biodisponibilidad de contaminantesSTG2-05. Aplicaciones de la geoquímica y la biogeoquímica en evaluación de riesgo y justicia ambientalSTG2-06. Educación en geoquímica y geocienciasSTG2-07. Fortalecimiento de las nuevas generaciones científicasSesión Técnica General 3. Economía moral y trabajoEste eje aborda el estudio del territorio, los recursos naturales y la energía desde una perspectiva científica y soberana, orientada, entre otros, hacia la transición energética.STG3-01. Petrología (ígnea, sedimentaria y metamórfica)STG3-02. Geoquímica de recursos mineralesSTG3-03. Investigación y desarrollo de nuevas tecnologías de minerales críticosSTG3-04. Geoquímica de isótopos y geocronología aplicada a recursos, energía y territorioSTG3-05. Geotermia e hidrocarburos en contexto de transición energéticaSTG3-06. VulcanologíaSTG3-07. PetroquímicaSTG3-08. GeoarqueologíaSesión Técnica General 4. Desarrollo sustentableEste eje concentra las investigaciones relacionadas con la protección del ambiente, la gestión integral del agua y el saneamiento de geosistemas, como pilares del desarrollo sostenible.STG4-01. Hidrogeoquímica e hidrogeologíaSTG4-02. Geoquímica marinaSTG4-03. Procesos contaminantes en cuencas y cuerpos de aguaSTG4-04. Interfases suelo–agua–sedimentoSTG4-05. Saneamiento de geosistemasSTG4-06. Geoquímica en la ingeniería ambientalSTG4-07. Geoquímica fundamental aplicada a sistemas ambientalesSTG4-08. Química analítica para monitoreo, trazabilidad y control ambientalSesión Técnica Transversal 1. Igualdad sustantiva y derechos de las mujeresSTT1-01. Perspectiva de género en las ciencias de la TierraSTT1-02. Ética, inclusión y diversidad en la cienciaSesión Técnica Transversal 2. Innovación pública para el desarrollo tecnológico nacionalSTT2-01. Geoinformática y aplicaciones GISSTT2-02. Modelación geoquímica e hidrogeológicaSTT2-03. Inteligencia artificial, big data y modelación predictivaSesión Técnica Transversal 3. Derechos de los pueblos y comunidades indígenas y afroamericanasSTT3-01. Ciencia participativa con enfoque territorialSTT3-02. Gestión ambiental y del agua con pertinencia culturalSTT3-03. Desigualdades socioambientales y territorialesComunidadEl congreso reúne a personas investigadoras, estudiantes y profesionistas provenientes de las principales universidades y centros de investigación de México, así como a invitados internacionales.Envío de resúmenesPara participar como ponente en el congreso, envía una contribución en formato de resumen corto (<350 palabras), resumen en extenso (<8 cuartillas) o artículo (<20 cuartillas).CommitteesComité científicoNadia Valentina Martínez Villegas (IPICYT), PresidentaAna Elizabeth Marín Celestino (IPICYT), STG1. Gobernanza con justicia y participación ciudadanaJanete Morán Ramírez (IPICYT) y Eliseo Hernández Pérez (IPICYT), STG2. Desarrollo con bienestar y humanismoPablo Dávila Harris (IPICYT) y Geoffrey Lerner (IPICYT), STG3. Economía moral y trabajoJosé Alfredo Ramos Leal (IPICYT). STG4. Desarrollo sustentableClaudia Lizbeth Rocha Estopier (IPICYT), STT1. Igualdad sustantiva y derechos de las mujeresJuan Alberto Velázquez Zapata (IPICYT) y José Tuxpan Vargas (IPICYT), STT2. Innovación pública para el desarrollo tecnológico nacionalLorena Elisa Sánchez Higueredo (IPICYT), STT3. Derechos de los pueblos y comunidades indígenas y afroamericanasComité organizadorNadia Valentina Martínez Villegas (IPICYT), PresidentaGladis Judith Labrada Delgado (IPICYT), Coordinadora de cursos precongresoJuan Alberto Velázquez Zapata (IPICYT), Coordinador de conferencias magistralesPablo Dávila Harris (IPICYT), Coordinador de los viajes de campoGeoffrey Lerner (IPICYT), Coordinador de premios y becasJosé Alberto Aguirre García (IPICYT), Coordinador de participación estudiantilLugar y fechasLa 36o edición se llevará a cabo del 12 al 17 de octubre de 2026 en las instalaciones del Instituto Potosino de Investigación Científica y Tecnológica (IPICYT), en San Luis Potosí, México.ContactoAngela Griselda Soto García, conageq2026@ipicyt.edu.mx

Los trabajos aceptados y presentados serán publicados como:Capítulos de libro con ISBN ó,Artículo en la revista Abstraction and Application de la Facultad de Matemáticas, Universidad Autónoma de Yucatán con ISSN: 2007-2635.Los autores cuyos trabajos sean publicados en Abstraction and Application, serán invitados a someter una versión extendida de la versión publicada considerando que difiera al menos un 40% en su contenido teórico, resultados experimentales y referencias bibliográficas, para una nueva revisión por pares y su eventual publicación en las revistas JCR, International Journal Of Combinatorial Optimization Problems And Informatics o Computación y Sistemas.TópicosSon bienvenidos todos los trabajos relacionados con la práctica docente, desarrollo de aplicaciones e investigación sobre los siguientes temas, pero no restringido a ellos:Big DataComputación CuánticaCloud ComputingComputación y SociedadCómputo CientíficoCiberSeguridadCiencia de DatosIngeniería de SoftwareInteligencia ArtificialIoTRealidad Virtual y AumentadaRobóticaSistemas DistribuidosSistemas EmbebidosTIC's en la EducaciónTópico Especial de "Investigación y Educación para la Salud"Atenta invitación a someter sus trabajos a revisión por pares para su inclusión en el Tópico Especial de Investigación y Educación para la Salud.Educación para la Salud.Cambio de Hábitos en la Sociedad.Investigación Educativa para la Educación, Prevención, Promoción y Mantenimiento de la Salud.Las TIC para la Educación, Prevención, Promoción y Cuidado de la Salud.Investigación en Fármacobilogía.Epidemiológicas de la Salud.
