Our goal is to establish a leading network that connects universities, research institutes, and scholars to promote scientific inquiry in areas such as Smart Solutions in Engineering, Efficiency of Production Systems, Advances Materials Engineering, Advances Mechanical Engineering, and Sustainable and Renewable Energy, among others. postings.conferenceName: IHM '26 - Explainable AI for End Users
postings.conferenceText: IHM '26 – XAI4U is a one-day workshop held during the 37th French-speaking Conference on Human-Computer Interaction (IHM’26), which will take place on October 20, 2026, in Lille, France.XAI4U – Explainable AI for End Users aims to explore how explainability can effectively support end users, going beyond purely technical solutions. The workshop focuses on how explanations can be designed, adapted, and evaluated through the lenses of Human-Computer Interaction (HCI), user experience (UX), and data visualization, to improve transparency, trust, and appropriation of AI systems.We welcome interdisciplinary contributions from HCI, AI, ML, UX, and visualization communities, including empirical studies, methodological proposals, design explorations, and critical perspectives. Presentations (15/20 min + Q&A) may be in French or English.Program09:00 – 09:30 Welcome and Introduction to the Workshop09:30 – 10:30 Session 1 – Presentation of ContributionsResearch papers, experience reports, demonstrations, ongoing work, or conceptual reflections.→ Each presentation will be followed by a discussion with the audience.10:30 – 11:00 Coffee Break11:00 – 12:30 Session 2 – Presentation of Contributions→ Each presentation will be followed by an open discussion with participants.12:30 – 14:00 Lunch Break14:00 – 15:30 Session 3 – Presentation of Contributions→ Each presentation will be followed by a discussion with participants.15:30 – 16:00 Coffee Break16:00 – 17:00 Session 4 – Presentation of Contributions→ Final presentations of the day followed by exchanges with the audience.17:00 – 17:30 Wrap-up and Open Discussion→ A collective discussion to reflect on the key ideas and insights from the day, share perspectives, identify future research directions, and explore opportunities for collaboration.Submission GuidelinesWe welcome short presentations related to the theme of AI explainability for end users. This includes, for example, the visualization of AI-generated data, the design of understandable interfaces, consideration of cognitive biases, or any other issue related to transparency, trust, or user appropriation of intelligent systems.Contributions on explanatory systems not directly related to AI may also be accepted if they help enrich the design of explanations in the context of XAI.research projects (ongoing or completed),tools, methods, or prototypes,conceptual or reflective work,design or UX explorations.Interested participants are invited to submit a title and a short abstract (maximum 1 page, references included) by Friday, September 18, 2026. postings.conferenceName: 2026 Intel Hardware Security Academic Award
postings.conferenceText: Topics: ai security cloud edge security foundational security resilient siliconCall for Papers: 2026 Intel Hardware Security Academic AwardIntel is pleased to share the 2026 Intel Hardware Security Academic Award guidelines and invite researchers to submit nominations by June 15th, 2026. This prestigious award is part of Intel’s commitment to foster advancements in solutions, methodologies and tools that enhance the industry’s ability to deliver more secure and trustworthy foundational technologies. Academic researchers are requested to submit a recently published paper that demonstrates novel research with a meaningful impact on the hardware security ecosystem, including but not limited to Intel’s own products. Researchers may also apply for a special Test of Time award for a paper published at least 10 years ago (i.e. prior to January 1st, 2016) that has demonstrated significant and lasting impact in the field.Winners will be announced at the Intel Academic Security Workshop in the fall of 2026. Selected winners will receive an exclusive invitation to a special event with a senior leader at Intel as well as being recognized on the “Chips and Salsa” Security at Intel podcast. All winners would have the opportunity to present to Intel security research and product development teams. Research articles will be featured on the INT31 Security Research at Intel website.Research Focus AreasSubmissions addressing the following focus areas are highly encouraged:AI for SecurityMethodologies and applications of analytics, machine learning, and advanced AI techniques to strengthen security robustness, threat detection and platform resilience across cloud and edge, including defenses against adversarial AI-driven attacks and accurate differentiation between true security issues and benign ones.Security for AITechniques to analyze, identify, and mitigate emerging threats in AI-enabled systems, including AI models, training and inference pipelines, workloads, accelerators, and Confidential AI technologies.Cloud to Edge SecurityThreat analysis, mitigations, and architectural improvements that strengthen security across cloud, data center, edge, accelerator, communication, and memory subsystems.Foundational Security TechnologiesAdvances in confidential computing, safety‑critical systems (e.g., robotics, cyber-physical systems), secure platform architectures, and next‑generation cryptography.Trusted Manufacturing and Supply Chain SecurityTechnologies that enhance security and transparency across semiconductor manufacturing and supply chains, enabling trusted production, integration and lifecycle management of products built on heterogenous chiplet architectures.Resilient SiliconArchitectural, microarchitectural, and circuit‑level innovations that improve silicon resilience against fault injection, side‑channel, and other physical attacks, as well as environmental and transient faults.Who QualifiesAny full time, tenured or tenure track (or equivalent) faculty member involved in research may make a submission. Intel will not, however, consider submissions by individuals residing in, or affiliated with, an academic institution located in a U.S. Government embargoed country. Intel also will not consider submissions by individuals on a U.S. Government sanctions list, including individuals affiliated with academic institutions on a U.S. Government sanctions list. postings.conferenceName: Innovations in Compiler Technology Workshop
postings.conferenceText: Topics: compiler programming languages formal verification software security================================================================Call for Papers ================================================================The 3rd workshop on Innovations In Compiler Technology (IICT) aims to bring together researchers, practitioners, and enthusiasts in the field of compiler technologies. The previous editions of the workshop were held in Bengaluru in September 2024 and September 2025. This edition of IICT is an iPLAN event and will be held on October 2-3, 2025 at the Indian Institute of Science (IISc) Bengaluru. More details about the workshop can be found at https://compilertech.org/.IICT focuses on the cutting-edge advancements in design, implementation, and optimization of compiler techniques as well as their applications on emerging software and hardware platforms. We invite research and practice papers from academia and industry for IICT-2026. We invite presentations on all aspects of programming languages and compilers, covering the classical compiler techniques, compilers for AI/ML, Domain Specific Languages, Web3, blockchain etc.Submission GuidelinesIICT-2026 will feature two tracks : Research Papers and Practice Papers. Proposals can be submitted under the form of an extended abstract (2– 4 pages), full paper (4 – 8 pages) for the Research Papers track. For the Practice Papers track, the submission can be in the form of extended abstract (1 page or more) or slides. In all cases, submissions should provide sufficient information for the program committee to judge the quality of the submission.Details on how to write high-quality submissions that articulate its contributions well can be found on the internet. See, for example:https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1878764915001606https://cambridge-research.org/blogs/how-to-write-a-research-paper/In addition, papers which were accepted / presented in premier venues (CORE A*/A Conferences) in the last 12 months can also be submitted and a limited number of these may be accepted for presentation in a special session. For this, submit the camera-ready version of the accepted paper, clearly indicating (as a footnote in the first page) the venue where the paper has appeared. All submissions will be reviewed by the Program Committee members and selection will happen in two steps: In the first step, a conditional acceptance will be provided. The second step requires the participants of conditionally accepted proposals to submit a 90-second video of their presentation which will be displayed as a teaser on the workshop website. The final acceptance will be provided based on the evaluation of the video presentations.Some of the submissions may be accepted for poster presentation rather than conventional presentations.As the workshop is intended as a forum for discussion of ongoing and emerging research, it will not publish formal proceedings. Consequently, the authors are free to submit extended or revised versions of their work to other conferences or journals.Important DatesWho should attend?Practitioners of compilersStudents and Researchers in the field of compilers, programming languages, and runtimeThose interested in using compiler and toolchain technology in novel and interesting waysPolicy on AI Generated ContentFor any use of AI tools during the development process or elsewhere, it is expected there is responsible disclosure regarding this in the submission and authors should be prepared for questions regarding the same. Further, authors are accountable for the content in their presentations and papers.The use of AI for grammar checks and syntactical rewriting is not required to be disclosed. ACM guidelines are here for further reference https://www.acm.org/publications/policies/frequently-asked-questionsList of TopicsThe below list is indicative.Novel Compiler OptimizationsDomain-Specific CompilersCompiler Frameworks and ToolsJust-In-Time (JIT) CompilationProgramming Language Design & ImplementationHardware-Software Co-designCompiler Verification and CorrectnessCompiler Education and OutreachCommitteesProgram CommitteeOrganizing CommitteeChair - Ashutosh Pandey (AMD)Co-Chair - Pradeep Kumar (NVIDIA)Co-Chair - Prerona Chaudhuri (NVIDIA)Co-Chair - Raveendra Kumar (TCS Research)VenueThe conference will be held at the AV Rama Rao Auditorium, IISc Bangalore on 2nd and 3rd of October.ContactIn case of any queries, reach out to the workshop organizers :ashutosh@compilertech.orgpradeep.kumar@compilertech.orgprerona.chaudhuri@compilertech.org

postings.conferenceName: Integration of Indian Knowledge Systems for Sustainable Development and Technological Transformation
postings.conferenceText: Topics: viksit bharat @2047 humanities futures governance political thought ethics economic thought rural humanities geography traditional sciences and innovation historiesIntegration of Indian Knowledge Systems for Sustainable Development and Technological TransformationOrganises by FACULTY OF ARTS & HUMANITIESMode: HybridDate: 26th & 27th February 2027Aligned With UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs): 4Venue: Kalinga University, Kotni, Near Mantralaya, Naya Raipur - 492101, ChhattisgarhThemeIntegration of Indian Knowledge Systems for Sustainable Development and Technological Transformation: Harnessing cultural heritage, social sciences and humanities as foundations for innovation, resilience, and national progress.Concept NoteThe global landscape is undergoing profound transformations driven by environmental challenges, technological advances, social inequalities, and shifting political dynamics. In this context, the pursuit of a sustainable future requires a multidisciplinary and inclusive approach — one that bridges the spheres of culture, society, and governance.This conference aims to create a vibrant platform for scholars, policymakers, practitioners, and community leaders to engage in critical dialogue about how we can transition toward a more just, resilient, and sustainable world. By examining the intersections of cultural narratives, social systems, and governance models, the event seeks to challenge conventional paradigms and propose innovative solutions to the complex challenges of our time. Culture shapes our values, beliefs, and behaviours; society reflects our collective organisation and resilience; governance determines how power and resources are distributed. This conference invites contributions that explore emerging trends, indigenous knowledge systems, participatory governance, social justice, and the role of education, media, and the arts in shaping sustainable futures.This Conference Aims ToThe key objectives of the conference are as follows:To promote the integration of Indian Knowledge Systems (IKS) into contemporary education, research, and innovation for holistic and sustainable development.To explore the relevance of traditional Indian knowledge in addressing modern challenges related to sustainability, environmental conservation, and societal well-being.To encourage interdisciplinary research that combines Indian Knowledge Systems with emerging technologies and scientific advancements.To provide a platform for scholars, researchers, academicians, policymakers, and industry experts to exchange ideas, research findings, and best practices on IKS and technological transformation.To identify innovative applications of indigenous knowledge in areas such as agriculture, healthcare, education, energy, environmental management, and entrepreneurship.To foster collaboration among educational institutions, research organisations, industries, and government agencies for the effective implementation of Indian Knowledge Systems in national development.To examine the role of Indian philosophical, ethical, and cultural values in promoting sustainable technologies, responsible innovation, and inclusive growth.To support the objectives of the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 by encouraging the integration of Indian Knowledge Systems into higher education curricula and research initiatives.To inspire young researchers and students to undertake innovative research that bridges traditional wisdom with modern science and technology.To develop policy recommendations and strategic frameworks for leveraging Indian Knowledge Systems to achieve sustainable development, technological advancement, and the vision of a self-reliant India (Atmanirbhar Bharat).Sub-themes:1. Viksit Bharat @2047 and Humanities Futures: Indian Knowledge Systems as cultural foundations for national vision, identity, and transformation.2. Governance, Political Thought, and Ethics: Traditions in administration, political science, ethics, and policy innovation.3. Economic Thought, Rural Humanities, and Geography: Self-reliance, rural transformation, and spatial-cultural development.4. Pedagogy, Educational Philosophy, and Literary Traditions: NEP 2020 enriched by Hindi and English literature, pedagogy, and cultural learning.5. Traditional Sciences and Innovation Histories: Knowledge trajectories, indigenous sciences, and historical innovation.6. Artificial Intelligence, Psychology, and Digital Humanities: Indian epistemologies in technology, cognition, and digital storytelling.7. Urban Development, Sociology, and Cultural Landscapes: Heritage-conscious, inclusive, and socially sustainable cities.8. Health, Wellness, and Embodied Traditions: Yoga, psychology of well-being, and holistic cultural practices.9. Climate Sustainability and Environmental Humanities: Resilience, ecological ethics, and cultural imagination.10. Law, Sports, and Media Narratives: Justice, indigenous games, sociology of sports, and cultural journalism.Submission GuidelinesPlease follow the guidelines below while preparing and submitting your work:The abstract should be 100 - 150 words.The full paper should be within 3000–3700 words, including title, abstract, main text, and references. It should include: Abstract, Keywords, Introduction, Literature Review, Methodology, Findings/Discussion, Conclusion, and References.Plagiarism must be below 10%. Authors must submit their own plagiarism report (Urkund / Turnitin / iThenticate / Drillbit). The review committee may conduct an additional plagiarism check.The paper title should align with the conference themes and sub-themes.All citations and references must follow the Harvard Author–Date referencing style with consistent formatting. Proper in-text citations corresponding to the reference list are mandatory.All papers should be in Times New Roman / Unicode-10, font size 12, with 1.5-line spacing.Authors must send abstracts in a Word Document only to arts.conference@kalingauniversity.ac.in by 25th December 2026.ParticipateDates, Registration & PaymentImportant DatesMilestone DateLast Date of Abstract Submission 25th January 2027Abstract Acceptance Notification 31st January 2027Last Date of Full-length Paper Submission 10th February 2027Last Date of Registration 19th February 2027Date of Conference 26th - postings.conferenceName: Workshop on Intelligent Information Retrieval and Agentic Systems for Specialised Domains
postings.conferenceText: Topics: agentic ai architectures rag and advanced information retrieval human in the loop ai frameworks for agentic systemsScopeThe rapid evolution of Large Language Models (LLMs) and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) techniques has opened numerous opportunities for developing intelligent systems capable of autonomous decision-making and adaptive information processing. However, applying these technologies to specialised domains—such as legal, medical, technical, and regulatory contexts—presents unique challenges that require domain-specific approaches, rigorous accuracy standards, and robust compliance frameworks. This workshop focuses on the intersection of advanced AI techniques and domain-specific applications within the broader context of ambient intelligence and artificial intelligence. As intelligent systems become increasingly embedded in our daily environments and routines, the need for accurate, contextually-aware, and trustworthy information retrieval becomes essential. There is a need to addresses the critical gap between general-purpose LLMs and the specialised requirements of professional domains, where errors can have significant legal, financial, or safety implications. By providing a platform for knowledge exchange between academia and industry, this workshop facilitates the transfer of cutting-edge research into practical application. We aim to bring together researchers working on theoretical advances in LLMs and RAG with practitioners deploying these technologies in real-world specialised domains. We invite a broad spectrum of contributions, ranging from original research and architectural proposals to industrial use cases and technological demonstrators. We specifically welcome work addressing the rigorous application of AI and emerging technologies in industrial environments, including research summaries and ongoing PhD studies.List List oof Topicsf TopicsRAG and Advanced Information RetrievalGraphRAG and knowledge graph integrationRetrieval optimisation for specialised corporaDomain-Specific Language ModelsFine-tuning and specialisation of foundation modelsFew-shot and zero-shot learning in specialised contextsEvaluation benchmarks for domain-specific LLMsAgentic AI ArchitecturesMemory systems for long-context reasoningTool use and external API integrationMulti-agent coordination and communicationFrameworks for agentic systems and benchmarkingDocument processing and analysis automationWorkflow automation using LLM agentsNatural language interfaces for complex systemsProcess optimisation through intelligent agentsApplications in Specialised DomainsHuman in the loop AITrust and transparency in automated systemsCollaborative intelligence between humans and AI agentsUser preference modelling and personalisationMetrics for RAG system performanceDomain-specific evaluation frameworksRobustness testing and adversarial scenariosOrganizing CommitteeFábio Silva, CIICESI, Escola Superior de Tecnologia e Gestão, Instituto Politécnico do Porto, PortugaRicardo Santos, CIICESI, Escola Superior de Tecnologia e Gestão, Instituto Politécnico do Porto, PortugaCesar Analide, Centro ALGORITM, Universidade do Minho, PortugalWebsitehttps://edition2026.isami-conference.net/tracks/workshops/iirasVenueThe conference will be held in Biblioteca Universitaria di Napoli (BUN)Ministero della Cultura and Scuola di Scienze Umane e Sociali in Naples, ItalyContactAll questions about submissions should be emailed to Fábio Silva <fas@estg.ipp.pt>

postings.conferenceName: The 15th International Joint Conference on Knowledge Graphs
postings.conferenceText: Topics: knowledge graph graph based ai agentic ai semantic webIJCKG 2026 CFP -----------------------------------------------------------------------IJCKG 2026: 15th International Joint Conference on Knowledge GraphsNovember 19–21, 2026, Bangkok, Thailandhttps://ijckg2026.aiat.or.thUPDATE!- Deadline Extension! Research / In-Use / Education Tracks- Abstract Submission Deadline: June 23,2026 (Extended) July 17, 2026- Full Paper Submission Deadline: June 30, 2026 (Extended) July 24, 2026- Acceptance Notification: August 26, 2026- Selected high-quality papers will be invited to submit extended versions to a special issue of the New Generation Computing journal (Springer), subject to the journal’s review process.-----------------------------------------------------------------------*** Overview ***The 15th International Joint Conference on Knowledge Graphs (IJCKG 2026) is an academic forum on Knowledge Graphs. The mission of IJCKG 2026 is to bring together researchers in the international Knowledge Graph community and related areas to present innovative research results and novel applications of Knowledge Graphs. IJCKG has evolved from the Joint International Semantic Technology Conference (JIST), a joint event for disseminating research results regarding the Semantic Web, Knowledge Graphs, Linked Data, and AI on the Web.IJCKG 2026 will take place in Bangkok, Thailand, hosted by the National Electronics and Computer Technology Center, Thailand and the Artificial Intelligence Association of Thailand.*** Theme ***The theme of this conference is “Knowledge Graphs for Agentic, Multimodal, and Retrieval-Augmented Intelligence”, which aims to explore the evolving role of knowledge graphs in next-generation AI systems. As artificial intelligence advances from standalone foundation models toward agentic, multimodal, and retrieval-augmented paradigms, knowledge graphs provide essential support for structured knowledge integration, semantic grounding, and explainable reasoning.This theme highlights the convergence of symbolic knowledge representation and data-driven AI, including the integration of knowledge graphs with retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), graph-enhanced large language models, autonomous and agentic systems, tool use, and multimodal learning. It also encourages research on knowledge representation, ontology engineering, knowledge acquisition, reasoning, and system-level integration for intelligent applications.The conference program will include workshops, keynotes, a frontiers and trends forum, industry forum, young scholars forum, evaluations and competitions, paper presentations, posters, and demos. We invite researchers from academia and practitioners from industry to share recent advances and practical experiences, fostering collaboration between research and application.In addition to research and application papers, IJCKG 2026 will continue to emphasize knowledge graph open resources to support data and system sharing in academia and industry, including knowledge graphs, ontologies, datasets, tools, APIs, frameworks, and standards.*** Tracks ***Research Track (Full paper, 15 pages)In-Use Track (Full paper, 15 pages)Education Track (Full paper, 15 pages)Poster and Demo Track (Short paper, 6-8 pages)Workshops Track (Full paper, 15 pages and Short paper, 6-8 pages)Industry Forum (TBA)Evaluation Challenges (TBA)*** Details of Tracks ***Research Track (Full Paper, 15 pages)The Research Track solicits original and unpublished research contributions on all aspects of Knowledge Graphs and related technologies. Submissions should present significant advances in theories, methodologies, algorithms, systems, applications, or evaluations related to Knowledge Graphs. Topics include, but are not limited to, knowledge representation, ontology engineering, knowledge acquisition, reasoning, graph analytics, knowledge graph construction and maintenance, semantic technologies, and the integration of Knowledge Graphs with AI technologies such as large language models, retrieval-augmented generation, multimodal AI, and agentic systems.In-Use Track (Full Paper, 15 pages)The IJCKG In-Use Track provides a forum to explore the benefits and challenges of applying Knowledge Graph technologies in concrete, practical use cases, in contexts ranging from industry to government and society (e.g., cultural heritage, astrophysics, biodiversity, medicine). The track aims to give a stage to applied works addressing real-world problems in which Knowledge Graph technologies have been employed, possibly in combination with machine learning, deep learning, large language models, and other AI techniques. The In-Use Track seeks submissions describing applied research as well as software tools, systems, or architectures that benefit from the use of Knowledge Graph technologies. Importantly, submitted papers should provide convincing evidence of the use of the proposed application or tool by the target user group, preferably outside the group that conducted the development and, more broadly, outside the Knowledge Graph research community.Education Track (Full paper, 15 pages)The IJCKG 2026 Education Track provides a forum for researchers and practitioners to explore the role of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Knowledge Graphs (KGs) in advancing education, learning, and educational technologies. The track aims to bring together innovative research on AI-driven learning environments, knowledge-enhanced educational systems, and emerging applications of generative AI, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and knowledge representation in education. The Education Track seeks submissions describing theoretical, methodological, and applied research, as well as educational tools, systems, and infrastructures that leverage AI and Knowledge Graph technologies. Topics of interest include AI in Education, Knowledge Graphs for Learning, Generative AI and Educational Applications, Knowledge Representation and Educational Infrastructure, and Evaluation, Interaction Design, and Community Resources for Education.Poster and Demo Track (Short Paper, 6-8 pages)IJCKG 2026 is pleased to invite submissions to the Poster and Demo Track, which complements the full-paper tracks of the conference. This track provides an opportunity to present late-breaking research results, ongoing research projects, innovative ideas, and work in progress. Poster and Demo presentations allow researchers to present their work directly to conference participants and receive valuable feedback on significant work in progress, cutting-edge research, emerging ideas, or systems that are best communicated through interactive or visual demonstrations. We welcome submissions relevant to the field of Knowledge Graphs, including but not limited to the topics covered by the IJCKG 2026 full-paper tracks. Suitable submissions include reports on ongoing or completed research, software systems, idea papers that introduce promising research directions, position papers presenting a bird's-eye view of a research topic, and PhD thesis abstracts.Workshop Track (Full paper, 15 pages; Short Paper, 6-8 pages)- RDM-KG 2026: Workshop on Research Data Management for Knowledge GraphsThe volume and complexity of research data continue to grow rapidly across scientific domains. Effective Research Data Management is now a prerequisite for reproducibility, collaboration, and compliance with FAIR (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable) data principles mandated by funding agencies worldwide. Knowledge graphs offer a powerful paradigm for organising, connecting, and querying heterogeneous research data, enabling richer metadata representations, provenance tracking, and cross-disciplinary integration. RDM-KG 2026 brings together the RDM and Knowledge Graph communities to address shared challenges, including data interoperability, ontology design, and data lifecycle management. For further details, please visit https://ijckg2026.aiat.or.th/call-for-workshops#rdm-kg- KGE-LLM 2026: International Workshop on Knowledge Graph Engineering in the Era of Large Language ModelsThis workshop focuses on the bidirectional synergy between LLMs for Knowledge Graph Engineering and Knowledge Graphs for Large Language Models. It aims to provide a forum for researchers and practitioners working at the intersection of these two rapidly evolving research areas. Large Language Models (LLMs) are transforming the way Knowledge Graphs (KGs) and ontologies are constructed, maintained, and utilized. LLMs offer new opportunities for knowledge acquisition, knowledge graph and ontology engineering, entity and relation extraction, semantic annotation, knowledge graph completion, and natural language interaction with structured knowledge. At the same time, Knowledge Graphs are becoming an essential foundation for enhancing the reliability, explainability, controllability, and factual grounding of LLMs and LLM-based AI systems through Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation (GraphRAG), knowledge-grounded reasoning, semantic memory, and agentic AI. We welcome contributions covering both directions of research: applying LLMs to knowledge graph and ontology engineering, and leveraging Knowledge Graphs to enhance LLMs and LLM-based AI systems. The workshop also encourages discussions on evaluation methodologies, trustworthy AI, benchmark datasets, practical deployment, and real-world applications. By bringing together researchers from the Knowledge Graph, Semantic Web, Ontology Engineering, Natural Language Processing, and AI communities, the workshop seeks to foster interdisciplinary discussion on how Knowledge Graph Engineering should evolve in the era of Large Language Models. For further details, please visit https://ijckg2026.aiat.or.th/call-for-workshops#kge-llmIndustry Forum (Full paper, 15 pages)The IJCKG 2026 Industrial Track provides a premier forum for industry practitioners, engineers, and applied researchers to showcase how Knowledge Graph technologies and AI are creatively deployed to solve complex, real-world problems while actively contributing to human flourishing. postings.conferenceText: Introduction for Call for Papers – ILCC 2026The Indian Lean Construction Conference 2026 (ILCC 2026) invites researchers, practitioners, industry leaders, policymakers, and students to contribute to the evolving dialogue on Lean Construction in India and beyond. Organised under the aegis of the Institute for Lean Construction Excellence (ILCE) and hosted by the Department of Civil Engineering, Indian Institute of Technology Bombay, ILCC 2026 continues the legacy of bringing together academia and industry to advance collaborative, efficient, and value-driven construction practices.Since its establishment in 2008, ILCE has played a pivotal role in promoting Lean Construction across India through conferences, workshops, training programmes, site-based implementation initiatives, and engagement with leading national and international experts. The Indian Lean Construction Conference has emerged as a key platform for sharing research, case studies, innovations, and practical experiences that support the transformation of the construction sector.The theme of ILCC 2026, “Beyond Efficiency: The Future of Lean Construction for a Digital and Sustainable Industry,” reflects the need to move beyond traditional productivity improvement and explore how Lean principles can enable a more resilient, technology-enabled, collaborative, and sustainable built environment. As the construction industry faces increasing pressures related to cost, time, quality, safety, sustainability, and digital transformation, Lean Construction offers a powerful framework to rethink project delivery, improve workflow reliability, reduce waste, enhance stakeholder collaboration, and create long-term value.ILCC 2026 welcomes original research papers, industry case studies, conceptual frameworks, implementation experiences, and technology-enabled solutions related to Lean Construction and its integration with digital technologies, sustainability, project management, supply chains, safety, quality, and infrastructure delivery. The conference aims to foster meaningful exchange between researchers and practitioners and to support the wider adoption of Lean thinking across the Indian and global construction ecosystem.Submission GuidelinesAll papers must be original and not simultaneously submitted to another journal or conference. postings.conferenceName: 10th International Symposium on Model-Based Safety Assessment
postings.conferenceText: Topics: model based system engineering reliability safety ai safetyIMBSA 2027 – Call for PapersPaphos, Cyprus, September 15-17, 2027International Symposium on Model-Based Safety and AssessmentModern safety-critical systems are changing rapidly. They increasingly combine physical components, complex software, connected services, autonomous behaviour and artificial intelligence. Machine learning, foundation models and intelligent agents are moving from experimental technologies into systems whose behaviour can have real consequences for people, infrastructure and society.At the same time, the fundamental challenge remains unchanged: how can we understand, predict and assure the behaviour of complex systems before failures occur?IMBSA brings together researchers, practitioners, tool developers and industry working on model-based and automated approaches to safety, dependability and assurance. The symposium provides a forum where advances in modelling, formal analysis, probabilistic reasoning, system engineering and safety assurance meet emerging developments in AI, autonomy and digital engineering.IMBSA 2027 invites contributions that advance the state of the art, demonstrate methods on realistic systems, report lessons from industrial practice, or challenge the community with important new problems.We particularly encourage work that connects established strengths of model-based safety engineering with the new assurance challenges created by increasingly complex, autonomous, adaptive and AI-enabled systems.A Conference Connecting Research, Technology and PracticeIMBSA is intended not simply as a venue for presenting papers, but as a meeting place for the model-based safety and assurance community.The symposium brings together:Scientific research, presenting new theories, methods and evidence;Industrial experience, showing how safety and assurance methods perform on real systems and where important challenges remain;Tools and demonstrations, allowing participants to experience new technologies rather than merely read about them;Emerging ideas, creating space for discussion of new system classes, new risks and new approaches to assurance.This interaction is particularly important today. Safety engineering must increasingly deal with systems that are interconnected, software-intensive, data-driven, adaptive and capable of making autonomous decisions. Traditional analysis remains essential, but it must evolve to address systems whose behaviour may change during operation and whose failure mechanisms cannot always be captured entirely at design time.IMBSA 2027 seeks work that helps shape that evolution.Topics of InterestWe welcome contributions on all aspects of model-based safety, dependability and assurance, including (but not limited to) the following broad themes.Model-Based Safety and DependabilityModel-based safety assessment and analysis; dependability modelling; failure and fault propagation; causal and probabilistic analysis; dynamic risk assessment; reliability, availability, maintainability and resilience; model-driven safety engineering.System Engineering, Architecture and Digital EngineeringSafety-aware architectures; integration of MBSE and safety engineering; cyber-physical and software-intensive systems; systems of systems; digital twins; simulation and co-simulation; model interoperability; engineering lifecycle integration.AI, Autonomy and Intelligent SystemsSafety and assurance of machine learning, generative AI, foundation models and AI agents; autonomous and adaptive systems; intelligent robotics; multi-agent systems; human–AI teaming; uncertainty and confidence assessment; explainability; runtime monitoring and assurance; AI-assisted safety engineering.Verification, Validation and Safety AssuranceFormal methods; model checking; specification and verification of safety requirements; simulation- and scenario-based verification; testing and fault injection; safety and assurance cases; continuous and runtime assurance; evidence generation; certification, standards and regulatory compliance.Safety, Security and ResilienceIntegrated safety and cybersecurity analysis; threat, hazard and risk modelling; adversarial behaviour; fault and attack propagation; resilience of interconnected and AI-enabled systems; trustworthy operation under uncertainty.Tools, Automation and Industrial ApplicationsSafety analysis tools and toolchains; automated generation and analysis of safety models; knowledge-based and data-driven approaches; benchmarks and datasets; industrial case studies and deployment experience across domains including aerospace, automotive, transport, robotics, energy, manufacturing, healthcare, maritime systems, critical infrastructure and other safety-critical applications.This list is deliberately broad. We particularly welcome submissions that cross traditional boundaries. For example, by combining model-based and data-driven techniques, connecting design-time analysis with runtime assurance, or applying established safety concepts to emerging forms of autonomy and AI.Types of ContributionsIMBSA 2027 solicits Regular Papers and Short Papers.Regular PapersRegular papers should present significant and original theoretical, methodological or practical results relevant to the model-based safety and assurance community and clearly explain their contribution beyond the state of the art.Suitable contributions include:Research papers presenting new theories, methodologies or technologies;Industrial and case-study papers demonstrating application at realistic or industrial scale;Tool papers presenting significant safety or assurance tools, platforms and integrated toolchains;Industrial experience papers describing deployment, evaluation, challenges and lessons learned;AI safety and assurance papers addressing the modelling, analysis, verification and assurance of AI-enabled, autonomous or intelligent systems.Regular papers should be 12–15 pages, including references and appendices, and will normally be presented orally at the symposium.Short PapersShort papers provide a more flexible route for bringing new ideas, emerging research, early results and practical technologies to the IMBSA community.They may present:Promising research directions or challenging open problems;Preliminary methods and results;Industrial applications and experience;New tools and demonstrations;Datasets and benchmarks;Emerging safety and assurance concepts;Provocative positions that can stimulate discussion within the community.Short papers should be 4–6 pages and may be presented orally or as a poster or demonstration, at the discretion of the Program Committee.Authors of accepted tool and demonstration papers will have the opportunity to present their technology live during an interactive conference session.Why Submit to IMBSA 2027?The challenges facing safety engineering increasingly sit between disciplines. A safety engineer may need to understand machine learning; an AI researcher may need to reason about hazards and assurance; a system architect may need models that remain connected to operational evidence; and industry needs methods that can move beyond laboratory demonstrations into credible engineering practice.IMBSA 2027 aims to bring these communities together.We therefore particularly encourage submissions that:Demonstrate genuinely new approaches to difficult safety and dependability problems;Connect models to evidence from real systems;Bridge research and industrial application;Integrate methods that have traditionally been studied separately;Make safety analysis more automated, scalable or usable;Address the assurance of AI-enabled and autonomous systems without abandoning rigorous engineering foundations;Identify important problems for which current methods are simply not good enough.Whether your contribution develops a new theory, analyses a complex industrial system, introduces a practical tool, tests an existing method under realistic conditions, or opens an important new research direction, we would like IMBSA 2027 to be the place where that work is discussed.Submission and PublicationRegular and short papers must be prepared using the Springer Lecture Notes in Computer Science (LNCS) templates.Submissions should be made through the IMBSA 2027 EasyChair system:https://easychair.org/my/conference?conf=imbsa2027All submissions will undergo full review by the Program Committee.Regular contributions are planned for publication in the Springer Lecture Notes in Computer Science (LNCS) proceedings.At least one author of each accepted paper must register for and participate in the conference for the paper to be included in the proceedings.Authors should consult the Important Dates section of the IMBSA 2027 website for the current deadlines for abstract submission, full paper submission, notification and camera-ready papers.Join the IMBSA Community in 2027As engineered systems acquire greater complexity, connectivity, intelligence and autonomy, assuring their behaviour is becoming both more difficult and more important.IMBSA 2027 invites the safety, dependability, systems engineering and AI communities to help define the methods by which these systems can be understood, assessed and ultimately trusted.We look forward to your contributions.Website: https://cyprusconferences.org/imbsa2027/

The conference welcomes contributions addressing how organizations can responsibly design, adopt, and govern intelligent technologies, strengthen resilience and trust, and reimagine management practices that balance performance, ethics, inclusion, and societal well-being in a rapidly changing global environment.Academics, doctoral students and practitioners are invited to submit: Research papers presenting important new findings in the field; Case studies describing new developments in management field; Academic papers dealing with medium or long-term trends and predictions. postings.conferenceName: 27th IMEKO TC4 Conference 2026 with Special TC11 Technical Session Measuring the Future
postings.conferenceText: Topics: measurement and instrumentation calibration traceability metrological standards advanced sensors signal processing systems e mobility automation emerging technologiesTC4 addresses theoretical and practical aspects of measuring electrical quantities using electronic instruments. Its work spans measurement accuracy, instrumentation design, calibration principles, uncertainty analysis, and digital metrology. Submission Guidelines All papers must be original and not simultaneously submitted to another journal or conference. The following paper categories are welcome: The IMEKO TC4 2026 Conference welcomes two categories of contributions. Authors are invited to choose the format that best suits the maturity and scope of their work. 1) Extended Abstract (1 page, not included in Proceedings) This category is intended for researchers who wish to present ongoing work, preliminary results, or ideas that are not yet ready for full-paper publication or will be published later. The length of the paper is exactly one page. Extended abstracts will not be included in the official Conference Proceedings. Extended abstracts cannot be considered for invitation to journal Special Issue. Accepted abstracts will be presented as oral or poster contributions during the Conference, depending on the decision of the Technical Program Committee. This format offers authors an opportunity to share ideas, gain feedback, and engage with the community without committing to a full manuscript. 2) Full Paper (4–6 pages, included in Proceedings) Full papers should present original research, significant technical developments, or innovative applications relevant to the TC4 or TC11 community. Manuscripts must be 4–6 pages in length and follow the provided formatting guidelines. Full papers will undergo peer review by the Technical Program Committee. Accepted full papers will be published in the official Conference Proceedings. Selected high-quality papers will be invited for extended publication in a Special Issue of selected peer-reviewed journals (ACTA IMEO, Measurement journal). This category is suitable for mature research results intended for archival publication and further dissemination within the IMEKO community. List of Topics Building on the long tradition of TC4 events, the 2026 conference will feature a technical program covering a wide range of topics, including: Measurement and instrumentation for electrical and magnetic quantities ADC and DAC modelling, characterization, and testing Calibration, traceability, and metrological standards Advanced sensors, signal processing, and measurement systems Applications in energy systems, e-mobility, industry automation, and emerging technologies Committees General Conference Chair Assoc. postings.conferenceName: Industrial Marketing and Purchasing Conference
postings.conferenceText: Topics: interaction business to business marketing industrial networks business relationships42nd Annual IMP Conference 2026, Ancona Call for Papers Polytechnic University of Marche – Department of Management, and The Industrial Marketing and Purchasing Group (IMP) are proud to welcome you to join the IMP Conference 2026 in Ancona, Italy, on 01-04 September 2026. The 42nd Annual IMP Conference invites contributions that examine how interaction and business networks evolve within changing business-to-business contexts, and how actors engage through networked relationships in both local and international settings. The overarching theme for this edition is: Building a Sustainable World Through Business Relationships and Networks The conference explores how interactions across networks can enable adaptation, resilience, and innovation in increasingly complex and uncertain environments. Scholars are particularly encouraged to address how relationships evolve in response to societal, technological, and policy changes. Tracks Papers may be submitted to the general track or to one of the eight Special Tracks.Click here to discover the Special Tracks. Submission of Abstracts Abstracts should be a maximum of 2 pages + references. Abstract submissions are done by using the online submission system: https://easychair.org/conferences?conf=imp26 Abstract submission form opens on December 1, 2025. The final date to submit your abstract is 20 January 2026. At the beginning of the submission process, after logging in as an author in EasyChair, please select “New Submission” from the menu at the top left. You are invited to submit the abstract either to the IMP2026 General Track or to one Special Tracks of your choice, (choose only one track). Fill in the author and affiliation details in the system only. For the Affiliation field, please indicate the full name of your institution and, where applicable, the department. The title and the abstract should be entered as plain text; they should not contain HTML elements. Type a list of keywords, one per line, to characterise your submission. Please specify at least three keywords. There is no need to upload a PDF file. The abstract must be pasted directly into the dedicated form. Submission of papers Deadline of Full paper submission: 15 April 2026 Paper submissions are done by using the online submission system https://easychair.org/conferences?conf=imp26 Paper submission is done by updating your accepted abstract submission by adding a pdf file of the paper to your submission. You can also update the abstract (in Easychair: update information) at this point. Please note: In case you submitted the abstract as a pdf file, you need to submit the abstract (again) by filling in the Easychair submission form (copy-paste). Only the anonymous paper can be submitted as a pdf file, not the abstract. Abstract and Paper editing instructions: Please adhere to the following criteria when preparing your submission: Abstracts should be a maximum of 2 pages + references. Abstracts and papers are subject to double-blind peer review. Please ensure all identifying information—names, affiliations, acknowledgements—is removed from the main document and file properties. Full papers should be: sent in PDF format, formatted for A4 paper, margins of 1 inch (2.54 cm), Times New Roman 12 pt, single-spaced, headings in capitals (main headings) or small caps (subheadings), centred, referencing style: Harvard (in-text and bibliography). Full papers should not exceed 8 pages, excluding references. Submissions are done by using the online submission system: https://easychair.org/conferences?conf=imp26.

postings.conferenceName: IMR Doctoral Conference 2027
postings.conferenceText: Topics: finance obhrm entrepreneurship marketingIMR Doctoral Conference 202711 & 12 January 2027Call for SubmissionsThe eighteenth IMR Doctoral Conference (IMRDC 2027) is being organised by IIMB Management Review (IMR) and the Office of the Doctoral Programme on 11 & 12 January 2027, at the Indian Institute of Management Bangalore (IIMB). IMRDC remains a benchmark doctoral colloquium in Management Sciences and seeks to facilitate collaborative work among researchers from across institutions in India and abroad. It provides a forum where focused feedback from eminent faculty could help improve the quality and rigour of doctoral student research. The conference has been commended by students and academics alike for the thorough and constructive feedback provided through its “one exclusive discussant per paper” format.IMRDC highlightsPremier doctoral (PhD) student conference in IndiaOpen to doctoral students from India and abroadThree rounds of rigorous reviewFull IMRDC scholarships covering domestic air travel, accommodation, and hospitality for the duration of the conference awarded to students whose papers are selected for final presentationOne exclusive discussant per selected paperInvited talks, workshops, and panel discussions by eminent academics.Papers presented at IMRDC have been published in top-tier journals.IMRDC winners from past conferences are now faculty at premier institutions such as the IIMs, London School of Economics, and IÉSEG, France, among others.We invite full paper submissions from doctoral students in Management across all areas, including Decision Sciences, Economics, Entrepreneurship, Finance & Accounting, Information Systems, Marketing, Organisational Behaviour & Human Resources Management, Production & Operations Management, Public Policy, and Strategy.The submissions will be reviewed by a Faculty Review Committee in multiple rounds, from which a set of papers will be selected for the final presentation and critiqued by invited discussants at the conference. Papers selected for the conference will be considered for publication in IIMB Management Review, subject to author approval and after completion of the journal’s required review process.An IMRDC Best Paper Award is given to a paper selected from among those presented at the conference, based on the decision of the Conference Chairs, the Discussants, and the Faculty Review Committee.Important DatesEligibility• The conference is open to doctoral students who have commenced research on their theses.• Only one paper per student is allowed; while co-authorship with faculty is permitted, the paper must be presented by the doctoral student at the conference.• The paper should not have been published, or accepted for publication, in any academic journal.Submission Guidelines1. Only full paper submissions will be considered. Papers should be submitted to https://imrdc2027.iimb.scholarit.net in the prescribed format.2. Submission Format· IMRDC-Scholarit submission page: When you make a submission, please ensure that all the fields in the information page are filled correctly. This would include:§ Title of the paper§ Keywords§ Topic/Subject area§ Abstract (200 words)§ Details of authors which include first name, last name, email, phone number, affiliation, and country.· Details of the authors’ names and afﬁliation should not appear in the main manuscript.· Full paper (without author identifiers):§ The full paper submission should contain the title of the paper, the 200-word abstract, the keywords, and clearly outlined literature, methodology and results sections. The paper should be uploaded as a pdf file.§ The paper, inclusive of tables, figures, references, and appendices, should be submitted as a single document and should not exceed 8,000 words.§ References should be in APA style (The following link can be used for guidelines - http://www.bibme.org/citation-guide/apa/ )§ The paper must be formatted in Times New Roman, 12-point font with double line spacing and 1" margin on all sides.§ Authors must submit a nomination letter from the concerned thesis advisor/faculty member. The letter should comment on the contribution of the paper to the student’s research agenda, especially for students not at an advanced stage of their research. The nomination letter should contain the signature and affiliation details of the advisor, along with the official seal.3. Submissions not following the above format will be desk rejected.4. Submissions will be put through an originality/plagiarism check. For details and regular updates about the conference, visit https://www.iimb.ac.in/imrdc2027/Conference Co-ChairsProfessor Maya Ganesh, Production and Operations Management, IIMBProfessor Varun Jindal, Finance & Accounting, IIMBAbout IIMB Management ReviewIIMB Management Review (IMR) is the flagship, quarterly journal of IIM Bangalore. It is a peer-reviewed, Elsevier Journal available through ScienceDirect®. IMR is listed on the Australian Business Deans Council (ABDC) Journal Quality List; and indexed on Scopus and the Emerging Sources Citation Index (ESCI). IMR is a Gold Open Access journal, supported by IIMB.Addressed to practitioners, researchers, and educators, IMR provides managerial insights in all the core business functions, with a special emphasis on emerging economies. We invite you to view the journal at https://www.iimb.ac.in/imr/index.php .Contact detailsFor any queries contact the Conference Secretariat at imrdc2027@iimb.ac.inAll email queries should bear the subject line: IMRDC 2027IMRDC Secretariat, IMR Editorial OfficeIIMB Management Review, Indian Institute of Management BangaloreBangalore - 560 076Phone: 91-80-26993099Website: https://www.iimb.ac.in/imrdc2027/

Located in Beacon Hill, a historic district known for its picturesque residential streets and landmarks such as the Massachusetts State House and Boston Common, the hotel sits adjacent to the main campus of Massachusetts General Hospital. With excellent access from Boston Logan Airport, South Station, Interstate 90/93, and US Route 1, it’s an ideal location for this international medical conference. The Liberty Hotel is also renowned for its unique history and stunning architecture. Originally built as the Charles Street Jail in 1851, it housed notable inmates including Malcolm X and former Boston Mayor James Michael Curley. After closing as a jail in 1990, the building was transformed into a luxury hotel in 2007. The property beautifully preserves many original architectural features, offering guests an inspiring experience and providing a unique setting for conferences like iMRI. postings.conferenceText: Topics: measurement efficiency innovation sustainabilityThe 2nd International Conference on Measurement Science and Applications (IMSA 2026) Venue: Eastin Grand Hotel Phayathai Date: 26 to 28 August 2026 Greetings It is my great honor to extend my warmest greetings to all distinguished participants, speakers, and guests at the 2nd International Conference on Measurement Sciences and Applications (IMSA 2026). On behalf of the National Institute of Metrology (Thailand), I am delighted to welcome you to this significant international forum. The theme of this year’s conference, "Measurements for Efficiency, Innovation, and Sustainability" reflects the pivotal role that measurement plays in shaping our collective future. Accurate and reliable measurements are not only fundamental to scientific discovery and industrial progress, but also essential to achieving broader global goals—ranging from clean energy and environmental protection to healthcare, digital transformation, and sustainable economies. Through this theme, IMSA 2026 emphasizes how measurement science drives innovation, enabling breakthroughs in advanced technologies, and how it supports sustainable development, ensuring that such progress benefits society responsibly and equitably. I hold great expectations that this conference will foster meaningful dialogue, spark new research collaborations, and strengthen the global metrology community. By bringing together experts from academia, industry, and policy, IMSA 2026 offers a unique opportunity to exchange insights and develop solutions that will address both current and emerging challenges. I wish all participants a fruitful and inspiring conference. May IMSA 2026 be a catalyst for advancing measurement science and for building a more innovative and sustainable future for all. Pol.Lt.Gen. Pornchai Suteerakune, Director, National Institute of Metrology (Thailand) Conference Themes and sub-themes “Measurements for Efficiency, Innovation and Sustainability” Topics of interest include, but are not limited to: Advanced materials Energy technology and energy transition Communication and sensing (quantum and conventional) Natural disaster and environmental crisis Food and health AI and robot Call for papers IMSA 2026 will bring together experts to explore how measurement science drives innovation, ensures quality, and addresses global challenges. We warmly invite your participation and contributions to this exciting event. For more information, please visit the IMSA 2026 website for more detailed guideline and instruction. postings.conferenceText: Topics: global macroeconomic uncertainty sustainable finance esg climate risk financial stability systemic risk geopolitics policy volatility economic fragmentationThe INCOSEF & EUMMAS A2S INTERNATIONAL CONFERENCE is an international conference co-organised by the Ho Chi Minh City University of Economics and Finance (UEF) and the European Marketing and Management Association (EUMMAS), to be held in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam, on 10–11 December 2026. The conference brings together scholars, industry leaders, and policymakers to discuss emerging issues in sustainable economics, finance, and technological development. With the theme “Global Social, Technological Development, Sustainable Economics and Finance in an Era of Geopolitical Uncertainty", the event serves as a dynamic platform for sharing research, fostering international collaboration, and connecting academic insights with real-world policy and business practices.Submission GuidelinesAll papers must be original and not simultaneously submitted to another journal or conference. The following paper categories are welcome.ABSTRACT SUBMISSIONWord Limit: 200–300 wordsRequired Information: Title, keywords, author(s)' name, affiliation, and email addressSubmission Portal: link (update)Review Process: All abstracts will be reviewed by the Scientific Committee to evaluate their relevance to the conference themes and academic quality. Authors will receive notification of acceptance and an invitation to submit a full paper.FULL PAPER SUBMISSIONWord Count: 4,000–7,000 wordsFormat: Publisher formatCitation Style: APA 7th editionSubmission Portal: link (update)Review Process: All submissions are reviewed by the Scientific Board through a double-blind peer-review process. Each submission is evaluated independently by at least two reviewers.FINAL MANUSCRIPT SUBMISSION (FOR PROCEEDINGS PUBLICATION)Format: Microsoft Word (.doc or .docx). PDF or Latex.Requirements: Manuscripts must follow the official submission guidelines and be written in clear, coherent English. Authors whose first language is not English are encouraged to seek professional editing support.REVIEW PROCEDURE The reviews were double-blind. Each submission was examined independently by at least 2 reviewers.The conference paper selection and peer-review process are conducted in accordance with international academic standards. The workflow consists of three stages: (1) abstract screening, (2) full-paper peer review combined with in-conference academic evaluation, and (3) score consolidation, final decision, and proceedings publication.Stage 1 – Abstract screening:Authors submit an abstract to register their proposed contribution. The Programme Committee conducts an initial screening to assess (i) relevance to the conference scope and themes and (ii) minimum academic quality, reflected in the clarity of objectives, expected contribution, and plausibility of the proposed approach. Approved abstracts are invited for full-paper submission.Stage 2 – Full-paper peer review and in-conference evaluation:Each full paper is reviewed by at least two independent subject-matter experts with relevant research experience. In parallel, the conference appoints a discussant (or designated evaluator) to provide a supplementary assessment and consolidate review requests to facilitate scholarly discussion. Eligible papers must be presented in the assigned technical session moderated by the Session Chair; presentation performance and subsequent discussion are recorded as part of the overall evaluation.Stage 3 – Score consolidation, final decision, and publication:The final decision is based on a composite score, calculated as the arithmetic mean of: (i) peer-review score(s), (ii) discussant score, and (iii) presentation score. Accepted papers must be revised in response to reviewer comments and in-conference feedback and resubmitted as camera-ready by the specified deadline. Camera-ready submissions are then checked for compliance with content and formatting requirements before being edited, compiled, and published in the conference proceedings.To ensure objectivity and reduce potential bias, reviewers were recused from handling submissions where any conflict of interest existed, including close professional or institutional relationships with the authors. The review process was conducted in accordance with established ethical standards to ensure fairness and transparencyNOTE: All submissions to the conference must undergo textual similarity screening to ensure academic integrity. Manuscripts with high similarity indices or suspicious textual overlap will be excluded from the review and evaluation process using one of the following tools: iThenticate, Turnitin, or CrossCheck.Publication OpportunitiesINCOSEF 2026 offers outstanding international publication opportunities for researchers across all career stages: Abstract submission (20/09/2026) | Notification of Acceptance/Rejection (30/10/2026) | Full paper submission (30/11/2026) | International Conference (10&11/12/2026) | Notification of Decision (20/01/2027) | Camera-ready submission (20/02/2027)CommitteesProgram CommitteeOrganising CommitteeScientific CommitteeSecretariat CommitteeContactAll questions about submissions should be emailed to incosef@uef.edu.vn, support@incosef.com, submission@incosef.com, and payment@incosef.comWhatsApp:+84 399 662 311 (Ms Thu); +0779366189 (Bao);+84 96 692 0858 (Ms Anh), +84 90 830 4416 (Ms Hang), +84 93 782 0940 (Ms Dung)

postings.conferenceName: Indian Academy of Management International Conference
postings.conferenceText: About INDAMIndian Academy of Management (INDAM) is an affiliate of the Academy of Management, USA, the premier body of management researchers and educators in the world. Established in 2007, INDAM to advance the creation and dissemination of knowledge on Indian businesses, organizations, and other institutions both within and outside India. It also seeks to influence management practices, business policy and education, and nurture the next generation of researchers and educators in India. To fulfil these objectives, INDAM provides a vibrant platform for scholars with an interest in India. It facilitates regular research conferences that enable academics to share ideas, exchange insights, and build collaborative networks. INDAM also serves as a bridge between Indian and international professional bodies and fosters meaningful engagement between scholars and practitioners. A key focus of INDAM is capacity building. The Academy organizes research development workshops, doctoral consortia, and professional training sessions designed to support early career researchers, including doctoral students and new faculty, in enhancing their research capabilities and publication skills.About Conference Theme - Reimagining Management in the Era of DisruptionAmid a rapidly shifting global landscape, the very foundations of management are being challenged by waves of disruption mainly on three intertwined fronts geopolitical uncertainty, technological breakthroughs, and sustainability imperatives. The rise of artificial intelligence, digital ecosystems, and borderless commerce in a geopolitically fractured world is redrawing the rules of strategy and operations, while societal demands for sustainability, agility, and inclusion are reshaping leadership norms. Across the Global South, these disruptions are broadly similar but are amplified by disparities in resources, infrastructure, and governance necessitating innovative, locally adapted management approaches that can both leverage growth opportunities and build long-term resilience. To thrive in this environment, organizations must reimagine management by embracing these disruptions not as a threat but as opportunity to reinvent business for a complex, interconnected, yet geopolitically fragile world. The disruptions reshaping management globally have particularly profound effects on India. Disruptions ranging from rapid technological advances to economic vulnerabilities have exposed businesses and communities to heightened uncertainty. These tensions coupled with geopolitical turbulence have significantly increased the operational risks for Indian enterprises, particularly in technology, service, manufacturing, and export sectors. Reimagining management in these contexts calls for a shift from narrow technological adoption to holistic strategies that integrate social inclusion, sustainability, and systemic agility to navigate complex, interconnected challenges more effectively. Thus, INDAM 2027 conference seeks to engage scholars and practitioners in deliberating cutting-edge insights on these pressing issues from a managerial lens with a specific focus on how management theory and practice can respond to these transformations.Submission GuidelinesAll papers must be original and not simultaneously submitted to another journal or conference. The following paper categories are welcome - extended abstract for Doctoral track and full paper for other tracks.List of TopicsTRACK 1: International BusinessReimagining global strategies in a world shaped by geopolitical flux, technological shifts, and fragmented markets. This track explores how firms rethink internationalization strategies, global value chains, cross-border governance, and digital international business models amid rising protectionism, regionalization, and institutional complexity.TRACK 2: Human Resource ManagementReinventing people practices for a technologically augmented, diverse, and fluid workforce. This track examines how organizations redesign talent acquisition, development, performance management, and employee well-being strategies in response to automation, demographic transitions, remote work, and post-pandemic realities.TRACK 3: Technology & Innovation ManagementHarnessing emerging technologies to build resilient, responsible, and future-ready innovation ecosystems. This track focuses on how digital technologies, artificial intelligence, and platform-based innovation reshape industries, innovation processes, and organizational capabilities, demanding new approaches to innovation leadership and governance.TRACK 4: 3D (Decarbonization, Democratization & Digitisation):This track explores the transformative 3D paradigm shaping contemporary economic and public policy landscapes. It invites research on how sustainable decarbonization, inclusive democratization, and rapid digitisation interact to influence economic growth, governance structures, institutional resilience, and broader societal well-being.TRACK 5: Supply Chain Management, Logistics & OperationsBuilding adaptive, digital, and sustainable operational systems to withstand continuous disruption. This track delves into supply chain resilience, risk management, sustainability transitions, and the integration of digital technologies to enhance agility, visibility, and robustness across global and domestic operations.TRACK 6: Organisational BehaviourUnderstanding evolving workplace behaviours, organizational cultures, and leadership norms in a disrupted world. This track explores how hybrid work arrangements, diversity and inclusion, digital collaboration, and technological mediation transform individual behaviour, team dynamics, and organizational effectiveness.TRACK 7: Strategic ManagementReframing strategic thinking to navigate volatility, seize digital opportunities, and build long-term adaptability. This track encourages research on dynamic capabilities, strategic renewal, ecosystem strategies, and managerial cognition, focusing on how firms make sense of uncertainty and sustain competitive advantage in unpredictable contexts.TRACK 8: Sustainability, Ethics & GovernanceEmbedding ESG principles as core drivers of resilience and long-term value creation in times of disruption. This track addresses how organizations respond to ethical dilemmas, regulatory pressures, stakeholder expectations, and governance challenges while aligning sustainability objectives with strategic and operational decision-making.TRACK 9: EntrepreneurshipExploring entrepreneurial responses to disruption and the emergence of new venture ecosystems in India and the Global South. This track focuses on how entrepreneurs identify opportunities, mobilize resources, leverage digital platforms, and innovate business models under conditions of uncertainty, institutional voids, and rapid change.TRACK 10: Financial MarketsExamining financial markets as critical mechanisms for resilience amid global disruptions. This track invites research on market responses to shocks, risk management practices, regulatory innovation, and digital finance, with an emphasis on market stability, inclusiveness, sustainable investment, and long-term economic recovery.TRACK 11: MarketingTransforming marketing strategies in response to empowered consumers, digital ecosystems, and fluid market behaviours. This track examines how firms adapt branding, customer engagement, analytics, and omnichannel strategies to build trust, loyalty, and resilience in rapidly evolving markets.Track 12: Sports Business & Management:On the back of India hosting the 2030 Commonwealth Games and future bids to host the Asian Games and Olympics, this track focuses on the nexus between Sports and Business and its successful Management. It would include the management of sporting activities and events; controversies increasingly affect sporting organisations, sponsors, broadcasters, and athletes; bidding and hosting mega sporting events; sports as a soft power; the bright and dark side of sport and business, among other topics.Pre- Conference Workshop & Doctoral:At INDAM 2027, the Doctoral Colloquium is designed to encourage participation from doctoral scholars currently enrolled in various management disciplines at recognized institutes/universities. Scholars will have the opportunity to present their ongoing research aligned with the conference theme, focusing on the evolution and relevance of time-tested management concepts in a rapidly changing world.Organizing CommitteeProf. Surender MunjalAston Business School Prof. Shubhabrata BasuIIM Indore Prof. Dipti Ranjan MahapatraIIM Sambalpur Prof. Shikha BhardwajIIM Sambalpur VenueThe conference will be held Indian Institute of Management Sambalpur Campus Basantpur, Goshala, Odisha, India. postings.conferenceText: Topics: neuro symbolic ai machine learning reasoning industrial applicationsTopics of InterestThe Industry Track of NeSy 2026 invites submissions detailing the practical applications of neuro-symbolic AI in real-world settings. We define neuro-symbolic AI applications as systems that:solve complex problems through the integration of deep learning and symbolic components;leverage symbolic knowledge bases and expressive metadata to enhance deep learning systems;support explainability and transparency through the use of background knowledge (XAI);employ machine learning techniques for graph-based reasoning.The focus is on deployed systems, business value, and the challenges of moving from research to production. Topics include, but are not limited to:Case studies and success stories of deployed neuro-symbolic systems in specific verticals, such as finance, healthcare, robotics, or manufacturing.Best practices and lessons learned from integrating neural and symbolic methods in an industrial context.Integration of Large Language Models (LLMs) with symbolic reasoning to improve factuality, planning, and reliability.Discussions on scalability, reliability, and other challenges encountered in production environments.Design and implementation of guardlines for deep learning systems using symbolic methods, such as mathematical reasoning.Reports on barriers to adoption and strategies for overcoming them.Benchmarks, datasets, tasks, and evaluation metrics or approaches with an industry context.Analyses of business value, ROI, and competitive advantages gained from using hybrid AI.Submission GuidelinesSubmission Portal: All submissions must be made through Easychair before the deadline. See submission link (soon).Page Limit: Industry track submissions should provide an overview of an industrial effort related to neuro-symbolic AI and need to be 3 to 4 pages, excluding references.Formatting: Please use the official LaTeX conference template.Content Focus: Submissions should describe a real-world application, its impact, and the lessons learned. Purely promotional or marketing material will be rejected.Review Process: All submissions must be anonymized to facilitate a double-blind review process.Presentation: The conference will be held in person. At least one author for each accepted paper must register and physically attend the conference to present their work.Proceedings: Accepted industry papers will be included in the official conference proceedings.Oganizing CommitteeGeneral ChairCatia Pesquita, Universidade de LisboaProgram committee co-chairsAlessandro Mileo, Insight SFI Research Centre for Data Analytics, Dublin City University, IrelandCogan Shimzu, Wright State University, USAAndrea Passerini, Università degli Studi di Trento, ItalyIndustry track co-chairsDaria Stepanova, Bosch Center for AI, GermanyPatrick Schneider, Siemens AG, GermanyContactAll questions about submissions should be addressed to organisers@nesyconf.org.
